item.title: Where did Texas football land in the AP Top 25 poll after beating Arkansas?
item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) takes photos with fans after the Longhorns' 45-3 win over the Arkansas Razorbacks at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Nov. 21, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football rose in the most recent Associated Press poll . The Longhorns leapt three spots to No. 5 following Saturday's 45-3 win over Arkansas . Texas now trails only No. 1 Georgia among SEC teams, and it sits directly ahead of SEC foes No. 6 Alabama and No. 7 Tennessee. Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian encourages quarterback Arch Manning (16) during senior day celebrations ahead of the Longhorns' 45-3 win over the Arkansas Razorbacks at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Nov. 21, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) The Longhorns, Crimson Tide and Volunteers are the three teams jostling for the chance to play Georgia in the SEC championship game Dec. 6. Each currently sit tied at 7-2 in the SEC, and each are expected to win their respective regular-season finales. The three-way tie would then create a tiebreaker determined by cumulative records of common conference opponents, in which Texas would advance by wins this weekend by LSU against Arkansas and Ole Miss vs. Mississippi State. PLAYOFF PUSH: Texas pounds Arkansas in home finale. Will the Longhorns play again in Austin this year? FAMOUS FACES: James Talarico fires cannon at today's game, Gov. Abbott attends, too The latest College Football Playoff rankings will be released Tuesday. The Longhorns were No. 5 in last week's CFP rankings, and are expected to rise to No. 4 this week following UCLA's loss at Michigan. The top four teams in the CFP receive first-round byes, while the No. 5 through No. 12 seeds will play first-round games Dec. 18 and Dec. 19. Here are the results from the AP poll: AP Top 25 heading into Week 13 RK Team REC PTS TREND 1 Georgia (56) 10-1 1711 - 2 Utah (12) 11-0 1662 - 3 Notre Dame (1) 10-1 1591 - 4 Miami 10-1 1491 1 5 Texas 9-2 1392 3 6 Alabama 9-2 1352 1 7 Tennessee 9-2 1317 2 8 Wake Forest 10-1 1264 2 9 Texas Tech 10-1 1166 2 10 UCLA 10-1 1156 6 11 BYU 9-2 1030 1 12 Indiana 9-2 958 6 13 Iowa 9-2 912 - 14 Oregon 8-3 865 - 15 USC 8-3 699 3 16 Arizona 8-3 665 3 17 Houston 8-3 570 3 18 Louisville 8-3 565 3 19 Oklahoma 7-4 341 NR 20 Florida 7-4 310 3 21 Liberty 10-1 294 1 22 Boise State 9-2 207 7 23 Ole Miss 7-4 200 2 24 Missouri 7-4 125 NR 25 Ohio State 7-4 112 9 Others receiving votes: New Mexico 95, Nebraska 90, UTSA 75, Kentucky 62, Washington 39, Louisiana Tech 31, North Dakota State 25, Toledo 22, Oklahoma State 12, Auburn 10, Air Force 7, Duke 2 What's this season's biggest upset? item.title: Broncos vs. Raiders: Live Fan Discussion
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 22: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos warms up prior to a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field At Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos will be looking to move to 8-2 on the year with a home win over the Las Vegas Raiders today. It figures to be an emotional day in the stands as fans mourn the death of the legendary Tom Jackson today. We all know how Jackson loved to beat the Raiders as a player, so what a chance to send a win and a mile high salute his way this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 2:25 p.m. Mile High time on Sunday, November 22, 2026 at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada. You can watch on CBS affiliates. The game will be called by Andrew Catalon (play-by-play), Logan Ryan (analyst), and AJ Ross (sideline). You can also check local Broncos radio network affiliate stations . Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Broncos vs. Raiders score predictions These two teams are in completely different situations. Vegas is looking to see what they have in their top overall pick while the Broncos are eying the AFC’s top seed and a Super Bowl run. This is a game the Broncos should win by double-digits, but this team also tends to play up or down to their opponent that day. However, coming off a bye week, I think they will be ready to roll on Sunday and finally give us a comfortable margin of victory. Broncos 33, Raiders 20 . Join the discussion in the comments section below. item.title: Packers Injury Report: 9 players limited on Sunday
item.description: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers had their entire active roster available to practice for the second day in a row. Considering how banged up the roster has been this season, that’s a massive win in itself. The Packers didn’t release a Saturday injury report, though, so Sunday was our first look at details on Green Bay’s injuries. Today, the Packers listed cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), linebacker Isaiah McDuffie (rib), receiver Bo Melton (thigh), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) as limited participants. Cisse, Melton and Moore were unable to finish the game against the Minnesota Vikings last week, while Franklin, Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Zeitler never suited up. The only surprise on this list is that McDuffie is still dealing with a rib injury, as he missed just one snap of action against the Vikings and came back into the game. Guard Aaron Banks is listed with only a knee injury, instead of both a knee and groin injury like in previous weeks, and was a full participant on Sunday. According to head coach Matt LaFleur, Banks is competing at both the left guard and right guard positions for playing time this week. If Banks doesn’t earn a starting role in practice, the assumption is that those gigs will go to Laken Tomlinson (left guard) and Kevin Zeitler (right guard). It’s also worth noting that teams are only allowed three padded practices from Week 12 to Week 18 of the NFL regular season. In preparation for their Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, the Packers decided to use a padded practice on Sunday. First Packers injury report before Wednesday's game pic.twitter.com/JBVxCHWYRU — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) November 22, 2026

item.title: How the 2027 Cubs Catching Situation Is Shaping Up
item.description: Aug 25, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Chicago Cubs catcher Miguel Amaya against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Cubs’ catcher situation has been an overlooked issue so far this offseason. Some of the Cubs’ biggest needs are pitching and outfield help, which is certainly true. However, catching has become just as crucial. The offseason is unpredictable, especially with a potential lockout coming, but Chicago needs to start planning. Current Cubs’ Catcher Option Miguel Amaya The most likely option to step up is Miguel Amaya . Last season, he served as Carson Kelly ‘s primary backup. Kelly was one of the Cubs’ option decisions earlier this offseason, when he declined his option. This was not a surprise, as he is one of the top free-agent catchers. That decision left Amaya as the frontrunner to be the Cubs’ catcher in 2027. Aug 25, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Chicago Cubs catcher Miguel Amaya against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Amaya has been solid over the past few seasons, but he hasn’t proven he can be a full-time starter. In 2026, he his .237 with six home runs and 28 RBI. His career has been pretty consistent, except in 2025, when he hit .281 in 28 games. As a rotation piece, it is not a bad choice. It’s hard to trust him as a full-time contributor, though. Joey Bart The Cubs’ catcher room does have a newcomer in Joey Bart . Chicago claimed him off the waiver wire after the Chicago White Sox parted ways with him. 2027 was a rough season, hitting .214 with four home runs and 13 RBI. His Major League career has not been great, as he has a .237 batting average and 32 home runs in seven seasons. Aug 6, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Chicago White Sox catcher Joey Bart (25) walks to the bullpen before the start of the game against the Boston Red Sox at Fenway Park. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images The 29-year-old has flashed potential, as in 2024 with the Pirates, when he hit 13 home runs and 45 RBI. The .265 batting average that season was the best of his career. He was once a highly thought-of prospect, being ranked as high as the 14th best prospect in 2020. But he hasn’t lived up to the hype. Now, Chicago hopes they will be able to use him in a timeshare with Amaya or Owen Ayers . At the bare minimum, he offers much-needed depth. item.content:encoded: Aug 25, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Chicago Cubs catcher Miguel Amaya against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Cubs’ catcher situation has been an overlooked issue so far this offseason. Some of the Cubs’ biggest needs are pitching and outfield help, which is certainly true. However, catching has become just as crucial. The offseason is unpredictable, especially with a potential lockout coming, but Chicago needs to start planning. Current Cubs’ Catcher Option Miguel Amaya The most likely option to step up is Miguel Amaya . Last season, he served as Carson Kelly ‘s primary backup. Kelly was one of the Cubs’ option decisions earlier this offseason, when he declined his option. This was not a surprise, as he is one of the top free-agent catchers. That decision left Amaya as the frontrunner to be the Cubs’ catcher in 2027. Aug 25, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Chicago Cubs catcher Miguel Amaya against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Amaya has been solid over the past few seasons, but he hasn’t proven he can be a full-time starter. In 2026, he his .237 with six home runs and 28 RBI. His career has been pretty consistent, except in 2025, when he hit .281 in 28 games. As a rotation piece, it is not a bad choice. It’s hard to trust him as a full-time contributor, though. Joey Bart The Cubs’ catcher room does have a newcomer in Joey Bart . Chicago claimed him off the waiver wire after the Chicago White Sox parted ways with him. 2027 was a rough season, hitting .214 with four home runs and 13 RBI. His Major League career has not been great, as he has a .237 batting average and 32 home runs in seven seasons. Aug 6, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Chicago White Sox catcher Joey Bart (25) walks to the bullpen before the start of the game against the Boston Red Sox at Fenway Park. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images The 29-year-old has flashed potential, as in 2024 with the Pirates, when he hit 13 home runs and 45 RBI. The .265 batting average that season was the best of his career. He was once a highly thought-of prospect, being ranked as high as the 14th best prospect in 2020. But he hasn’t lived up to the hype. Now, Chicago hopes they will be able to use him in a timeshare with Amaya or Owen Ayers . At the bare minimum, he offers much-needed depth. Owen Ayers Probably the fan favorite option, Ayers could fit into the 2027 plans. In 2026, he blew up and became Chicago’s second-best prospect . He was also in contention to be one of the Cubs’ September call-ups when the roster expanded. While that didn’t happen, he is still one of the Cubs’ prospects to watch next season. In 2026, Ayers rose from Single-A to Triple-A. Across the minor league system, he showed his pop at all three levels. His switch-hitter ability is something neither of the other catchers has, offering a strategic advantage. Of the Cubs’ catcher options, Ayers has the potential to be the best all-around. Knoxville Smokies’ Owen Ayers (6) during the Minor League Baseball game against the Columbus Clingstones on July 1, 2026, in Knoxville, Tennessee. Saul Young/News Sentinel / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images The 25-year-old catcher is a solid hitter who has proven to be able to have some pop in his bat. Additionally, one of the flashiest parts of his season was his efficiency at throwing out runners on the basepaths. It could be hard to thrust him into a major role in his first season, but he likely has to be considered. Whenever a season happens, it would be surprising if Ayers does not see time at the Major League level, even if it is in a rotation. How Carson Kelly Fits In Now, the three current options could be solid, but it should not stop Chicago from exploring other options. The front office should be looking at bringing back Kelly. The past few seasons, he has been the Cubs’ catcher, and it has been great. He may not be elite, but he is a good bat and works well with the defense. If they brought him back, it would likely be a short-term deal. To start the season, it would likely be Kelly and Amaya serving as the Cubs’ catcher duo, working the same way as they did this season. Chicago Cubs catcher Carson Kelly (15) hits two-run double during the ninth inning of their game against the Milwaukee Brewers Tuesday, September 8, 2026 at American Family Field in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. It gets interesting if he doesn’t come back. Chicago could roll with the three they have, but it is hard to feel excited about that option. If Ayers breaks out, he will cement himself as the team’s starter. But there would be pressure on all three, and the Cubs’ catcher position would be set to be the team’s biggest weakness. The Last Word While pitching and outfield help are the two biggest focuses, the Cubs’ catching position cannot be overlooked. They are too good a team to throw out anything less than solid play. The three current options could form a solid group, but bringing back Kelly would help solidify it. We may not get an answer anytime soon, but it is certainly a storyline to monitor. Main Photo Credit: Mark J. item.title: Best Case, Worst Case, and Most Likely Scenarios for the 2026-27 Badgers
item.description: MADISON, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 10: Owen Foxwell #15 talks with Head Coach Greg Gard of the Wisconsin Badgers during the second half of the game against the Fairfield Stags at Kohl Center on November 10, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images I waited longer than normal to do this piece because the 2026-27 Wisconsin Badgers carried more uncertainty than usual coming into the season, and I’m glad that I did. The first three weeks of the campaign have been both illuminating and disturbing. One big question coming in was whether or not Wisconsin would effectively replace two premium scorers, John Blackwell and Nick Boyd. We all saw an offensive drop-off on the horizon, but how steep it would be was far from certain. There were also associated worries about the lack of a slasher, along with spooky point guard depth. And, of course, fitting the pieces together has always been a puzzle for Greg Gard, who has generally completed it deftly in recent years. Winning the lottery three consecutive transfer portal cycles certainly helped matters. But as we inch toward December, it is clear that this version of the Badgers is flawed and, after losing Jack Janicki to what could be a long-term injury, is now down a major rotational player. Other issues have been a lack of consistent scoring and an oddly passive start from pre-season All-Big Ten senior Nolan Winter, who is very talented but has, at times, looked disinterested on his way to a tepid 8.0 points per game so far , due to a lack of shooting volume. And while they have had nice moments, it’s hard to be overly excited about portal headliner Eian Elmer or new point guard Owen Foxwell . Both have offered flashes, especially Foxwell, but it hasn’t been nearly enough. Making matters worse, transfer big man Victory Onuetu has looked, at times, unplayable. Adding to all this, nobody appears so far to be better than they were in 2026-27, and team cohesion seems broken, as best evidenced by a forgettable two games at the Baha Mar Championship , where the Badgers were outplayed by two decent but not special teams in Seton Hall and Murray State, never looking comfortable and shooting awfully. So, the quick take is that things are not good for Gard’s team and there is a legitimate reason to worry about an awful season. But Gard is a very good coach, and I suspect he will have some fixes to raise the squad’s suddenly troubling floor. However, nothing is a given. After seeing the first stretch of games for Wisconsin, here are my Best Case, Worst Case, and Most Likely scenarios for the 4-2 Badgers the rest of the way. Best Case I’ll admit right here at the outset that I’m relying as much on track record and projectables, including Winter rounding into form and Foxwell/Elmer settling in under the brighter lights in Madison, as anything else. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images I waited longer than normal to do this piece because the 2026-27 Wisconsin Badgers carried more uncertainty than usual coming into the season, and I’m glad that I did. The first three weeks of the campaign have been both illuminating and disturbing. One big question coming in was whether or not Wisconsin would effectively replace two premium scorers, John Blackwell and Nick Boyd. We all saw an offensive drop-off on the horizon, but how steep it would be was far from certain. There were also associated worries about the lack of a slasher, along with spooky point guard depth. And, of course, fitting the pieces together has always been a puzzle for Greg Gard, who has generally completed it deftly in recent years. Winning the lottery three consecutive transfer portal cycles certainly helped matters. But as we inch toward December, it is clear that this version of the Badgers is flawed and, after losing Jack Janicki to what could be a long-term injury, is now down a major rotational player. Other issues have been a lack of consistent scoring and an oddly passive start from pre-season All-Big Ten senior Nolan Winter, who is very talented but has, at times, looked disinterested on his way to a tepid 8.0 points per game so far , due to a lack of shooting volume. And while they have had nice moments, it’s hard to be overly excited about portal headliner Eian Elmer or new point guard Owen Foxwell . Both have offered flashes, especially Foxwell, but it hasn’t been nearly enough. Making matters worse, transfer big man Victory Onuetu has looked, at times, unplayable. Adding to all this, nobody appears so far to be better than they were in 2026-27, and team cohesion seems broken, as best evidenced by a forgettable two games at the Baha Mar Championship , where the Badgers were outplayed by two decent but not special teams in Seton Hall and Murray State, never looking comfortable and shooting awfully. So, the quick take is that things are not good for Gard’s team and there is a legitimate reason to worry about an awful season. But Gard is a very good coach, and I suspect he will have some fixes to raise the squad’s suddenly troubling floor. However, nothing is a given. After seeing the first stretch of games for Wisconsin, here are my Best Case, Worst Case, and Most Likely scenarios for the 4-2 Badgers the rest of the way. Best Case I’ll admit right here at the outset that I’m relying as much on track record and projectables, including Winter rounding into form and Foxwell/Elmer settling in under the brighter lights in Madison, as anything else. But a reversion to the mean is a tough thing to use as the basis of an optimistic projection. It’s possible to imagine the rotation solidifying, perhaps with more Jackson Ball, who is raw but clearly talented, and the parts we’ve all seen do good things before, like Austin Rapp and Braeden Carrington, stepping up. It’s not crazy to believe Gard settles things down and forges a solid, tough Big Ten team. But one with a high upside like last year’s seems all but impossible. Prediction: 19-13, No. 10 seed in NCAA Tournament Worst Case This one pains me to write but I need to be real here. Even presuming health, early returns showing a team full of role players and secondary scorers, with no rim challenging slashers and some periodically questionable defensive and rebounding lapses, spells deep trouble vs the Big Ten. While there are still some bright spots, especially at home, more often than not this team gets chewed up and spit out by better teams, leading to Greg Gard’s first losing season in a decade and a renaissance year for the Fire Gard Army. Prediction: 12-20, no postseason. Most Likely Case I hope that I’m ultimately humbled by this prediction, but I’m finding an unusually difficult time being optimistic about this team based off early returns. It simply isn’t as good as recent squads and I’m not going to pretend this isn’t the case just because I hold the coach in high regard. Yes, I see improvement for Winter and some of the rest going forward, and as noted, Ball is an intriguing young talent. But not having a reliable scorer like Blackwell will simply cap this team’s ceiling. There’s no way to sugar coat it. There will be several nice moments and, I’m sure, an upset or two, but at this point it is looking like the worst Badger team in a decade and that one had All-Big Ten star Ethan Happ . This season will almost certainly be Gard’s biggest challenge since taking over for Bo Ryan in late 2015 and even an expanded NCAA Tournament looks unlikely. Prediction: 16-16, NIT.

item.title: Mark Pope addresses challenges of roster turnover in modern era, building teams for ‘one-year run’
item.description: Since Mark Pope took over at Kentucky in 2024, the transfer portal has been key to building his rosters. He brought in nine players upon his arrival before adding six transfers during both the 2025 and 2026 cycles. The portal landscape has changed recruiting across college sports since transfers gained immediate eligibility. To Pope, it adds to the challenges of roster construction in the modern era, but he also sees some bright spots. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage In the era of player movement, Pope said it’s harder to tell whether a key piece will still be around through multiple years. While Trent Noah is still with the Kentucky program from Pope’s first class, he knows “one-year runs” are becoming more apparent as teams build rosters. “We’re in this era where seasons are standalones,” Pope told Jon Rothstein . “Of course, with everything that changes, you miss some things – you used to be putting together a roster that you would plan out who is going to be around, a particular player, three years from now. There was something great about that and seeing guys grow that way. Listen, we still have third-year guys here at Kentucky that have been with me the whole time. SUBSCRIBE to the On3 NIL and Sports Business Newsletter “But you really, in some essence now, are reconstructing a team for a one-year run in some senses. There’s some really magical things about that, too, is knowing that this is your shot. This is the year that you guys get to be together as an entire group. Taking advantage of every moment and the pace of growth and development and learning, those challenges are really exciting, too.” Last year’s Kentucky team drew plenty of headlines with a roster that reportedly cost upward of $22 million. The Wildcats went 22-24 and lost to Iowa State in the second round of the NCAA Tournament, one year after making it to the Sweet Sixteen in Pope’s debut season. As a result, the 2026-27 season became a big one for Mark Pope in Year 3 at his alma mater, where he was a captain for Rick Pitino . There have been some missteps through the early going, though, as Kentucky heads into Thanksgiving with a 4-2 record. The Wildcats lost to Kansas by 20 points during the Champions Classic and, most recently, had a rough second half in a 90-76 loss to Indiana . They also found themselves in a nail-biter against Northern Arizona at Rupp Arena before coming away with the 78-77 win.

item.title: How Steelers' Loss to Eagles Impacts AFC North Chances, Playoff Path
item.description: How Steelers' Loss to Eagles Impacts AFC North Chances, Playoff Path originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Steelers had a fairly favorable path to end a decades-long losing streak in Philadelphia. Instead, they lost their 12th consecutive road game against the Eagles, dating back to 1965. Facing an Eagles team down to its third quarterback, dealing with injuries and subtractions at multiple key positions, the Steelers fell 19-16 on Sunday, unable to generate much offense due to five sacks against Aaron Rodgers and an ejection for DK Metcalf. As Joe Milton did just enough to get Philadelphia a win — its first since Week 2 — Pittsburgh dropped a game that could have some lasting consequences in its AFC playoff chase. Here's an updated look at the Steelers' path to the playoffs after losing to the Eagles. MORE: Why DK Metcalf Was Ejected From Steelers' Week 11 Game How Steelers' Loss Impacts AFC North Chances, Playoff Path Sunday's loss dropped the Steelers to 6-4, which still isn't a bad spot to be in for the AFC wild-card chase. However, considering the Eagles matchup was one of the more favorable ones Pittsburgh had remaining, it does tighten things up a bit for Mike McCarthy's team. Had the Steelers won in Week 11, they would have remained tied in the win column with the Bengals at the top of the AFC North, with Cincinnati still to play on Monday night against the Commanders. Instead, if the Bengals beat Washington on Monday, the Steelers will be two full games behind in the division. Here are the updated AFC North standings: 1st: Bengals (7-2, vs. Commanders on Monday night) 2nd: Browns (6-4, Week 11 bye) 3rd: Steelers (6-4, L vs. Eagles) 4th: Ravens (4-7, L vs. Panthers) While Baltimore's loss keeps the Ravens off the Steelers' heels, the path to beating the Bengals for the division title is getting tougher. Chances are, Pittsburgh will be vying for AFC wild-card contention in the weeks to come. In that race, the Steelers remain in a playoff spot. Even with their loss, the Steelers are at the AFC's No. 7 seed, trailing the sixth-seeded Browns, but still ahead of the 5-5 Patriots. Here's a look at the AFC wild-card picture: No. 5 Seed: Broncos (7-2, vs. Raiders on Sunday) No. 6 Seed: Browns (6-4, Week 11 bye) No. 7 Seed: Steelers (6-4, L vs. Eagles) No. 8 Seed: Patriots (5-5, Week 11 bye) No. 9 Seed: Texans (4-6, W vs. Colts) No. 10 Seed: Raiders (4-6, vs. Broncos on Sunday) The fortunate news for Pittsburgh is that it isn't a packed playoff picture in the AFC right now — only three non-division leaders are above .500, and the Steelers remain one of them. item.title: Steelers OLB Alex Highsmith seen in boot after loss vs. Eagles
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images Steelers outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was seen in a walking boot after suffering an ankle injury in the Steelers’ 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles Sunday afternoon, multiple reporters posted after the game. Alex Highsmith just walked past me wearing a walking boot on his left foot. — Jenna Harner (@JennaHarner11) November 22, 2026 Highsmith suffered the injury on his second sack of the game, when his left ankle appeared to get rolled up on while bringing down Eagles quarterback Joe Milton. Highsmith was initially ruled questionable to return in the first quarter, and later ruled out. #AlexHighsmith @steelers By limited video, rolled up on left ankle Worry for high ankle sprain, hope for mild Friendly fire Officially QUESTIONABLE ankle pic.twitter.com/YPaCQoaXTz — David J. Chao – ProFootballDoc (@ProFootballDoc) November 22, 2026 Highsmith’s injury left an already shorthanded Steelers outside linebacker down another top player. Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) was ruled out ahead of Pittsburgh’s game in Philadelphia, leaving the Steelers with T.J. Watt, Jack Sawyer, and the recently signed K.J. Henry at the position for the rest of the game. With new Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy rarely providing injury updates to the media, Highsmith’s status will primarily be monitored in the team’s injury reports ahead of a Black Friday game in Week 12 against the Denver Broncos.

item.title: Travis Kelce continues to make history while helping the Chiefs win
item.description: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense continued its tear through the middle of the schedule with another 30-plus-point performance, their sixth of the season, against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11. The Chiefs got off to a hot start, and so did tight end Travis Kelce, who caught two touchdowns in the first half. He finished with a team-high seven targets and six catches for 74 yards. Travis Kelce's first half: – 2 touchdowns – 6 catches – 74 yards AZvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o8MqVtHAcY — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 They were the 109th and 110th scores of Kelce’s career, both in his 100th game at Arrowhead Stadium (he became the fourth Chiefs player ever to do so). The touchdowns pushed him up the list with the all-time greats, surpassing former New England Patriots legend Rob Gronkowski (108) to rank third in history, behind Tony Gonzalez (115) and Antonio Gates (118). Kelce’s fifth touchdown of the season matched or exceeded his year-long totals from each of the last three years 2026: 5 2025: 5 2024: 3 2023: 5 At age 37-048, Travis Kelce is the 2nd-oldest tight end with 2+ touchdowns in a game since 1970, behind only Tony Gonzalez. pic.twitter.com/0Ezs233KM1 — Screwball NFL (@ScrewballNFL) November 22, 2026 Kelce also became the second-oldest tight end ever to score two touchdowns in a game (since 1970), less than 200 days younger than Gonzalez when he topped the list in 2013.

item.title: ‘Honestly baffling’ – Josh Allen blasted for ‘reckless’ performance in Bills win vs Dolphins
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images Josh Allen has come under fire for his shaky performance in the Buffalo Bills’ 26-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon. Allen threw two interceptions against the Bills’ struggling AFC rivals and a third was overturned for a penalty. The 30-year-old finished the game with just one passing touchdown as Buffalo improved to 10-1. His display raised questions about his passing form, particularly against a Dolphins team sitting at 1-8 before this weekend. NFL fans voiced their frustration with the Bills star on social media. One wrote: “Josh Allen hasn’t been a good passer or processor from the pocket for like two years now. It’s honestly baffling.” Another added: “ Josh Allen throwing 3 first-half INTs is nasty work. That 3rd one got called back, but man, the decision-making has been reckless”. A third posted: “Josh Allen has 2 picks against a bad team, with a bad defense, that is also starting a backup QB.” Others were equally unimpressed, with one fan describing it as “Probably Josh Allen’s worst game since the Dolphins game last year.” Another declared: “Safe to say Josh Allen won’t win MVP this season.” Allen has remained in the MVP conversation largely because of Buffalo’s impressive record and his contributions as a runner. He has scored 11 rushing touchdowns this season, but his passing numbers of 14 touchdowns and nine interceptions have not been as convincing. A win is a win for Buffalo, but Allen will need more consistent performances through the air if he is to remain a serious contender for the MVP award. The Bills now face a blockbuster Thanksgiving weekend showdown against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. item.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft order: What Titans, Dolphins losses in Week 11 mean for No. 1 pick race
item.description: Updated 2027 NFL Draft order: What Titans, Dolphins losses in Week 11 mean for No. 1 pick race originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As playoff races heat up around the NFL, the race to the bottom is on as well. The league's worst teams are jockeying for position in the 2027 NFL Draft, whether they know it or not, and the wheeling and dealing that sent first-round picks around the NFL has added another layer of intrigue to the mix. Now that every team has at least one win, the field is as crowded as ever near the top of the draft order. Here's an updated look at the 2027 NFL Draft order in Week 11, with the Chargers finally out of the top spot. MORE: How 2026 Chargers compare to Jim Harbaugh's worst seasons NFL Draft order 2027 This is how the first round of the NFL Draft would shake out of the season ended today: Pick Team Record 1 Titans 1-9 2 Dolphins 1-9 3 Chargers 1-8 4 Jets 2-8 5 Jets (from IND) 3-8 6 Cardinals 3-8 7 Eagles 3-7 8 Buccaneers 3-7 9 Saints 3-7 10 Falcons 3-7 11 Ravens 4-7 12 Commanders 3-5-1 13 Texans 4-6 14 Raiders 4-6 15 Jets (from DAL) 5-6 16 Patriots 5-5 17 Browns (from LAR) 6-4 18 Seahawks 6-4 19 Panthers 5-5 20 Browns 6-4 21 Steelers 6-4 22 Cowboys (from GB) 6-4 23 Giants 5-3-1 24 Broncos 7-2 25 Bengals 7-2 26 Eagles (from JAX) 7-2 27 Vikings 7-2 28 Titans (from CHI) 8-2 29 Chiefs 8-2 30 Lions 8-2 31 49ers 8-1 32 Bills 9-1 MORE: Why Fernando Mendoza is big winner of NFL flex decision NFL Draft prospects Here's a look at the top 10 prospects in the 2027 NFL Draft, based on the NFL Mock Draft Database 's consensus big board: Rank Player Position School 1 Jeremiah Smith WR Ohio State 2 Colin Simmons EDGE Texas 3 Drew Mestemaker QB Oklahoma State 4 Leonard Moore CB Notre Dame 5 Dylan Stewart EDGE South Carolina 6 CJ Carr QB Notre Dame 7 Jordan Seaton OT LSU 8 Charlie Becker WR Indiana 9 Darian Mensah QB Miami 10 Chris Cole LB Georgia While there isn't a consensus No. 1 pick, many consider Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith to be the best player in the draft. A quarterback-needy team, however, could look at Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker or Notre Dame's CJ Carr considering the value of the position. In the NIL era, there is also the question of which players might return to school. That question focuses particularly on Mestemaker, as reports have indicated he could lean toward a return to school amid an impressive season at Oklahoma State. item.title: Watch Bucky Irving and Vita Vea’s absurd touchdown celebration that has fans going wild
item.description: Watch Bucky Irving and Vita Vea’s absurd touchdown celebration that has fans going wild originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Vita Vea usually creates highlights on the defensive end, but he went viral for a different reason on Sunday against the Detroit Lions . In the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' loss to the Lions, Vea was a key part of one of the Buccaneers' touchdowns. However, it wasn't the score that went viral, as it was Vea's role in Tampa Bay's touchdown celebration that became a huge hit among fans. In a year that has seen its fair share of creative touchdown celebrations, very few players can celebrate the way that Vea and Bucky Irving did. Take a look at why fans loved this celebration so much. MORE : Colston Loveland produces highlight-reel play vs. Saints Bucky Irving and Vita Vea’s touchdown celebration With the Buccaneers down at the goal line, Tampa Bay brought on Vita Vea to serve as an extra blocker, and the play worked. Irving used Vea's block to get into the endzone for the score, cutting the Lions' lead to three points. After scoring, Irving and Vea teamed up for a unique celebration, as Vea lifted his jersey and allowed Irving to slap him in the stomach. The greatest celly doesn’t exi- 📺: #TBvsDET on FOX 🎉: @BudLight https://t.co/chfUoUpiVU — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) November 22, 2026 HANG IT IN THE LOUVRE 🖼️ https://t.co/m4zaCXT5NI — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) November 22, 2026 Vea is usually known for his success as a defensive tackle, using his size to both stop the run and rush the passer. Every once in a while, the Buccaneers use Vea as a blocker on offense, and Irving seemingly wanted to get Vea involved in the touchdown celebration as well. It's not a surprise that Irving and Vea's celebration went viral, as Vea is a bit of a fan favorite nationally across the NFL. item.title: Viral redheaded UCLA cheerleader’s boyfriend has cheeky response to her new fans
item.description: Sharlize True Trujillo was crowned Miss California 2026 in June. But it took a video of her dancing during a UCLA Bruins football game going viral for her to reach celebrity status. The video showed Trujillo, Quillan Casem, and Hayleigh Liu dancing as part of UCLA’s cheer team when the Bruins played Illinois earlier this month. It received over 30 million views on X and was one of the most discussed sports stories that weekend. Transferring to UCLA pic.twitter.com/Z2ed3jAGMT — Buckeye HQ (@RealisticBuck) November 14, 2026 It also made many wonder whether Trujillo was single . And she has been very clear about her relationship status on social media, as she is, in fact, dating an actor named Jackson Dollinger. These two often post about each other on Instagram. Trujillo made a post on Nov. 13 that prompted a message from Dollinger. Sharlize True Trujillo speaking on an episode of the “two be continued… podcast. (YouTube/@two be continued…) The post showed a side profile of her during a UCLA game and was captioned, “game day let’s bring it home all the way ucla”. Dollinger commented on the post, writing, “that’s my girl”. “hi love,” Trujillo wrote back. Sharlize True Trujillo dancing during a UCLA Bruins football game. (Instagram/@sharlizetrue_) Sharlize True Trujillo and her boyfriend, Jackson Dollinger, pose for a photo. (Instagram/@sharlizetrue_) All of Trujillo’s social media posts get a lot of comments, especially since that aforementioned video went viral. Many people are hoping that she becomes a Los Angeles Rams cheerleader in the future, given that she is a senior at UCLA right now. Regardless of what Trujillo’s future holds, she has already cultivated quite the fan base that she can capitalize on.

item.title: Jeeno Thitikul three-peats at CME, earning another $4 million check
item.description: NAPLES, FL — Jeeno Thitikul has become a money-making machine . The world No. 2 became the first player to three-peat at the CME Group Tour Championship . In fact, she's the first player to win a tournament three times in a row since Inbee Park won what's now the KPMG Women's PGA from 2013-2015. "I have no word(s)," said Thitikul after a closing 7-under 65 at Tiburón Golf Club. "The only word I have to Terry [Duffy] is just don't change the course until I retire. Don't change it. I mean, it's just me and the course. I think we just really best friend." With the victory, 23-year-old Thitikul surpasses Annika Sorenstam on the all-time money list with $24,292,858. She earned nearly half of that in only three starts at the CME. Nelly Korda, who played alongside Thitikul on Sunday, finished solo third after a closing 68. The world No. 1 also surpassed Sorenstam with a $550,000 check. Korda's career earnings are now $22,972,616. Thitikul, who joined the tour in 2022, accomplishes the feat in only 104 career starts. Sorenstam retired in 2008 and won 72 times. She reached $22,583,693 in 308 starts. "It's really hard to go up against Jeeno out here," said Korda, who has yet to win at Tiburon. "I feel like she just has this place figured out." A victory today at CME would've put Korda into the LPGA Hall of Fame as she's only one point shy of the 27 required to gain entry. Korda won four times this season, including the U.S. Women's Open and Chevron Championship , to earn the LPGA's Rolex Player of the Year award. She battled a two-way miss throughout the week at Tiburon. "You know, still being able to compete when I didn't even really feel like I really had my trust in like a B or C game," she said of her main takeaways. "So just proud of the way that I fought this week to kind of give myself a chance." Thitikul won a tour-leading five times on the LPGA this season, including at home in Thailand, the place where it all began. She made 18 cuts in 20 starts, finishing in the top 10 a total of 11 times (including the wins). The CME check brings her season earnings to $6,923,458. Though she has yet to win a major, Thitikul has said many times throughout her career that her primary goal was to take care of her family, and she has provided well with 12 career victories. Thitikul finished at 24 under for the tournament, two strokes ahead of Japan's Aki Iwai (65), who still won $1 million for her efforts. Miyu Yamashita, a three-time winner this season, won the Vare Trophy with a 69.453 scoring average. Both Nelly Korda and Haeran Ryu were ineligible after failing to meet the required minimum number of rounds. "I'm truly honored to receive this award," said Yamashita. "My goal this season was to win, and I managed to win three times, so overall it's been really good year for me." Beth Ann Nichols is a senior writer for Golfweek covering the LPGA and all things women's golf. Follow her on X/Twitter (@GolfweekNichols). This article originally appeared on Golfweek: J

item.title: Dodgers make moves ahead of MLB Lockout, await Tarik Skubal's decision
item.description: Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park on September 14, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. LOS ANGELES — With Thanksgiving around the corner, baseball fans have plenty to be thankful for. However, the holiday season isn't the only thing on the minds of Major League Baseball fans. The countdown to a potential MLB lockout is quickly approaching, with the current collective bargaining agreement set to expire on December 1, 2026. Unless the league and the MLB Players Association reach an agreement, a lockout could begin December 2, bringing baseball's offseason to a sudden halt. The biggest disagreement between the two sides remains the possibility of introducing a salary cap and floor. Owners are pushing for a system that could take effect as early as 2028, while the MLBPA continues to strongly oppose a salary cap. The timing couldn't be worse for teams looking to make significant offseason moves. With Opening Night scheduled for March 24, 2027, and spring training traditionally beginning in mid-to-late February, a prolonged labor dispute could put the upcoming season in jeopardy. If negotiations stretch too far into March, the possibility of losing regular-season games, or even threatening the full 162-game schedule, becomes increasingly real. For now, teams still have an opportunity to make trades and sign free agents before a potential lockout prevents further transactions. And the Dodgers aren't wasting any time. Following a disappointing end to their season, in which they were swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS, the Dodgers are looking to make the necessary adjustments to get back to the top of baseball. They have already made moves to improve their roster, but the biggest decision of their offseason could still be ahead. item.content:encoded: Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park on September 14, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. LOS ANGELES — With Thanksgiving around the corner, baseball fans have plenty to be thankful for. However, the holiday season isn't the only thing on the minds of Major League Baseball fans. The countdown to a potential MLB lockout is quickly approaching, with the current collective bargaining agreement set to expire on December 1, 2026. Unless the league and the MLB Players Association reach an agreement, a lockout could begin December 2, bringing baseball's offseason to a sudden halt. The biggest disagreement between the two sides remains the possibility of introducing a salary cap and floor. Owners are pushing for a system that could take effect as early as 2028, while the MLBPA continues to strongly oppose a salary cap. The timing couldn't be worse for teams looking to make significant offseason moves. With Opening Night scheduled for March 24, 2027, and spring training traditionally beginning in mid-to-late February, a prolonged labor dispute could put the upcoming season in jeopardy. If negotiations stretch too far into March, the possibility of losing regular-season games, or even threatening the full 162-game schedule, becomes increasingly real. For now, teams still have an opportunity to make trades and sign free agents before a potential lockout prevents further transactions. And the Dodgers aren't wasting any time. Following a disappointing end to their season, in which they were swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS, the Dodgers are looking to make the necessary adjustments to get back to the top of baseball. They have already made moves to improve their roster, but the biggest decision of their offseason could still be ahead. Dodgers Bring Home Southern California Native Royce Lewis Sep 16, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Twins first baseman Royce Lewis (23) in action against the New York Yankees in the third inning at Target Field. Matt Blewett-Imagn Images Sep 16, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Twins first baseman Royce Lewis (23) in action against the New York Yankees in the third inning at Target Field. The Dodgers have made another significant addition to their infield, acquiring Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins in exchange for right-handed pitcher Bobby Miller and catching prospect Francisco Espinoza. Lewis, 27, gives the Dodgers another versatile offensive option with the ability to play both third base and first base. The Southern California native appeared in 125 games for Minnesota last season, hitting .227 with 15 home runs and 57 RBIs. Across five major-league seasons, all with the Twins, Lewis has compiled a .246/.302/.429 slash line with 61 home runs and 213 RBIs in 383 games. Although his 2026 numbers weren't particularly eye-catching, Lewis has demonstrated the offensive potential that made him the No. 1 overall selection in the 2017 MLB Draft out of JSerra Catholic High School in San Juan Capistrano. His best season came in 2023, when he hit 15 home runs, drove in 52 runs and recorded a career-best 2.4 fWAR. Defensively, Lewis appeared in 42 games at third base and 80 games at first base last season, giving the Dodgers additional flexibility as they continue to shape their infield. For the Dodgers, the move represents an opportunity to add a former top prospect who still has considerable upside. Having grown up in Southern California, Lewis also gets the opportunity to return home and contribute to a Dodgers team with championship expectations. Minnesota, meanwhile, received a former first-round pick in Miller and a young catching prospect in Espinoza. Miller, 27, made three appearances for the Dodgers last season, finishing 1-0 with a 3.68 ERA. Over parts of four seasons with the Dodgers, he posted a 14-8 record with a 5.37 ERA. The Dodgers originally selected Miller 29th overall in the 2020 MLB Draft out of the University of Louisville. Espinoza, 19, also heads to Minnesota after spending the 2026 season between the Arizona Complex League and Ontario. He appeared in 46 games, batting .317 with three home runs and 25 RBIs. Since signing as an international free agent out of Acarigua, Venezuela, on January 15, 2024, Espinoza has put together an impressive start to his professional career, compiling a .315/.425/.412 slash line with four home runs and 47 RBIs. While the Dodgers are giving up two players with potential, Lewis provides an immediate major-league option who could help address their infield needs. Tarik Skubal Remains the Biggest Piece of the Offseason Puzzle Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers pitches against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park on September 14, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. Robert Sloter - The Sporting Tribune Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers pitches against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park on September 14, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. While the Lewis acquisition gives the Dodgers another offensive weapon, the biggest storyline surrounding their offseason remains Tarik Skubal. The reigning elite-level left-handed pitcher is one of the most sought-after names in this year's free-agent market, and the Dodgers remain among the teams pursuing his services. Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, has indicated that his client is likely to make a decision before the potential December 2 lockout. That puts additional pressure on interested teams to get their offers in place before the deadline. According to reports, the Dodgers are among just four teams that have met with Skubal in person over the past week. The other three are the New York Mets, Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres. The Mets have reportedly presented Skubal with a nine-year offer worth approximately $400 million, setting a significant benchmark for the remainder of negotiations. For the Dodgers, adding Skubal would represent another major investment in an already ambitious roster. The Dodgers have consistently prioritized building a dominant pitching staff, and bringing in a pitcher of Skubal's caliber could dramatically strengthen its rotation heading into 2027. However, the Dodgers aren't the only organization willing to spend big. The Mets have demonstrated their willingness to make an aggressive financial commitment, while Toronto and San Diego also remain in the conversation. Skubal's decision could have a domino effect across the free-agent pitching market. Once one of the biggest names comes off the board, other starting pitchers could begin receiving more serious offers as teams adjust their offseason plans. With a potential lockout looming, the timing of his decision could be just as important as the contract itself. The Dodgers now face a critical question: Are they willing to make the financial commitment necessary to bring Skubal to Los Angeles, or will they look elsewhere to strengthen their rotation? Alex Call Returns on $2.175 Million Deal Alex Call #12 of the Los Angeles Dodgers on the field prior to a game against the Tampa Bay Rays at George M. Steinbrenner Field on August 01, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. Robert Sloter - The Sporting Tribune Alex Call #12 of the Los Angeles Dodgers on the field prior to a game against the Tampa Bay Rays at George M. Steinbrenner Field on August 01, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. While the Dodgers continue pursuing major upgrades, they also took care of an important piece of their roster earlier this week. Outfielder Alex Call agreed to a one-year, $2.175 million contract for the 2027 season, avoiding arbitration and remaining in Los Angeles rather than entering non-tender free agency. Call is entering his second full season with the Dodgers after being acquired from the Washington Nationals at the 2025 trade deadline. Although he hasn't received an everyday role, Call has provided the Dodgers with another dependable outfield option wh

item.title: Serie A | Atalanta 4-4 Inter: Incredible comeback, Pio hat-trick not enough
item.description: Serie A | Atalanta 4-4 Inter: Incredible comeback, Pio hat-trick not enough Atalanta completed an incredible comeback from 3-1 down to hold Inter 4-4 despite Pio Esposito’s first Serie A hat-trick, as Charles De Ketelaere and Franck Kessie snatched a point. The Nerazzurri had Curtis Jones, Lautaro Martinez and John Stones only fit for the bench after several weeks out , with Ange-Yoan Bonny and Aleksandar Stankovic injured. La Dea saw their disastrous run of two points from four rounds ended by a 1-0 win away to Monza going into the break for international duty. The treatment room was finally emptying out, leaving only Isak Hien and Odilon Kossounou, as Gianluca Gaetano and Thomas Kristensen were back in the squad . However, Marco Carnesecchi pulled out in the warm-up with a knee injury, replaced by Marco Sportiello. Atalanta have a famously poor record against Inter, scraping six draws and 11 defeats since the 4-1 victory here in November 2018. See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog. BERGAMO, ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Players of Atalanta BC and players of FC Internazionale line up ahead the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and FC Internazionale at New Balance Arena on November 22, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) Hakan Calhanoglu’s early effort from the D was deflected wide, but the deadlock was broken when two Nicolò Barella crosses in a row were deflected, a poor Giorgio Scalvini clearance allowing him to put the second into the path of Pio Esposito to sweep in first-time from nine yards. It should’ve been 2-0 when Marcus Thuram mistimed his jump on a Carlos Augusto cross to waste the free header. Moments later, Josep Martinez had to parry the Nikola Krstovic strike at the near post, then stuck out a boot to clear the loose ball from Charles De Ketelaere. Sportiello made a tricky double save on Thuram’s angled drive and the Pio Esposito follow-up, but on the resulting corner, the Italy international was allowed a free header to complete the brace. BERGAMO, ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Francesco Pio Esposito of FC Internazionale celebrates after scoring his team’s opening goal during the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and FC Internazionale at New Balance Arena on November 22, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) It came at a price, because Calhanoglu limped off with a suspected flexor strain, replaced by Petar Sucic. Just as Inter were getting back into shape, Atalanta got one back. Nicola Zalewski pulled back from the left for Eljif Elmas, whose first attempt was charged down, but he rifled the second into the roof of the net from 12 yards. Benjamin Pavard’s header was deflected inches wide, but Pio Esposito completed his first ever Serie A hat-trick after the restart when sent through by an inspired Thuram slide-rule pass to beat Sportiello from 10 yards. BERGAMO, ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Francesco Pio Esposito of FC Internazionale scores his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between Atal

(Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) Hakan Calhanoglu’s early effort from the D was deflected wide, but the deadlock was broken when two Nicolò Barella crosses in a row were deflected, a poor Giorgio Scalvini clearance allowing him to put the second into the path of Pio Esposito to sweep in first-time from nine yards. It should’ve been 2-0 when Marcus Thuram mistimed his jump on a Carlos Augusto cross to waste the free header. Moments later, Josep Martinez had to parry the Nikola Krstovic strike at the near post, then stuck out a boot to clear the loose ball from Charles De Ketelaere. Sportiello made a tricky double save on Thuram’s angled drive and the Pio Esposito follow-up, but on the resulting corner, the Italy international was allowed a free header to complete the brace. BERGAMO, ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Francesco Pio Esposito of FC Internazionale celebrates after scoring his team’s opening goal during the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and FC Internazionale at New Balance Arena on November 22, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) It came at a price, because Calhanoglu limped off with a suspected flexor strain, replaced by Petar Sucic. Just as Inter were getting back into shape, Atalanta got one back. Nicola Zalewski pulled back from the left for Eljif Elmas, whose first attempt was charged down, but he rifled the second into the roof of the net from 12 yards. Benjamin Pavard’s header was deflected inches wide, but Pio Esposito completed his first ever Serie A hat-trick after the restart when sent through by an inspired Thuram slide-rule pass to beat Sportiello from 10 yards. BERGAMO, ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Francesco Pio Esposito of FC Internazionale scores his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and FC Internazionale at New Balance Arena on November 22, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) Elmas threatened to reduce the gap again on a De Ketelaere knockdown, but Thuram went on the counter and was brought down by Scalvini for a yellow card. Jones made his first appearance since September 19, but Atalanta got back into it when Josep Martinez fingertipped a Krstovic header over the bar, then was beaten by a very similar attempt by De Ketelaere on the resulting corner. They had barely finished celebrating when Thuram tried to surprise Sportiello from the tightest of angles, Davide Zappacosta got back to clear off the line, but then jutted out an elbow as he fell on it, pushing the ball away. A penalty was awarded and a yellow card rather than red, as Petar Sucic swept the spot-kick into the near bottom corner. BERGAMO, ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Francesco Pio Esposito of FC Internazionale celebrates with his teammate Marcus Thuram of FC Internazionale after scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and FC Internazionale at New Balance Arena on November 22, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) Lautaro Martinez also made his comeback after five weeks out, but Josep Martinez used his legs to deny De Ketelaere a tap-in from the Giacomo Raspadori pull-back. It wasn’t over, as De Ketelaere then controlled the Jonathan Rowe cross, let it bounce, and smashed his shot into the roof of the net from 12 yards with the aid of a slight deflection for 3-4. Josep Martinez had to rush outside his area to clear from Krstovic on the counter, then made a sensational one-handed save to keep out the Mario Pasalic scorcher at the 87 th minute. Alessandro Bastoni jumped with his arms raised and the De Ketelaere header struck it for a penalty in the final minute. Franck Kessie converted sending Martinez the wrong way for 4-4, the second time Atalanta have had this result in Bergamo this season after another chaotic thriller with Frosinone on October 25. Atalanta 4-4 Inter P Esposito 16, 32, 52 (I), Elmas 35 (A), De Ketelaere 72, 81 (A), Sucic pen 76 (I), Kessie pen 91 (A)

item.title: Ian Wright Urges Arsenal to “Just Go and Get” £67m Winger in January
item.description: Ian Wright Urges Arsenal to “Just Go and Get” £67m Winger in January Ian Wright has urged Arsenal to make a January move for RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa, insisting that Mikel Arteta’s side need further attacking reinforcements despite their position at the top of the Premier League. The former Arsenal striker was left frustrated by the Gunners’ attacking options during Saturday’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle United, particularly the lack of impact from the substitutes introduced in the second half. Wright Wants Arsenal to Strengthen Their Attack Speaking to Sky Sports, in comments reported by the Evening Standard , Wright made his feelings about Arsenal’s January priorities clear. “We have been linked with Nusa at RB Leipzig. If think we should just go and get him.” Wright believes Arsenal need additional quality on the left wing and in attack, arguing that the club should be ambitious in the transfer market rather than relying on their existing options. He was particularly unimpressed by Christos Tzolis following his introduction against Newcastle and also questioned whether Viktor Gyokeres is providing sufficient competition for Kai Havertz. With Arsenal chasing another Premier League title and hoping to make progress in Europe, Wright clearly feels attacking reinforcements could make the difference. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) Arsenal Have Already Identified Nusa as a January Target Of course, Nusa is hardly a new name to Just Arsenal readers. We previously reported that Martin Odegaard could help Arsenal land the Norwegian winger , with the Gunners potentially benefiting from the relationship between the two international teammates. The 21-year-old has also acknowledged the rumours linking him with Arsenal , although he insisted his focus remains on playing football for Leipzig. However, the biggest obstacle could be the transfer fee. As we reported earlier this week, Arsenal could have to pay as much as €90 million to persuade the Bundesliga club to part with their highly rated winger. Other reports have suggested a valuation closer to €80 million, approximately £67 million, making Nusa a potentially expensive January addition. Nevertheless, Wright’s comments highlight a growing concern about Arsenal’s attacking depth, particularly when games become difficult and Arteta needs something different from his substitutes. With the Gunners six points clear at the top, the question is whether Arsenal should invest heavily in January to strengthen their advantage or trust the players who have taken them this far. Gooners, would Antonio Nusa be worth spending £67 million on in January, or should Arsenal prioritise other areas of the squad? item.title: Week 11 Game Recap: Bucs fall to 3-7; Behind coaching woes
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Trevor Nowaske #53 of the Detroit Lions sacks Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the fourth quarter at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Knee deep in the midst of one of the most surreal playoff races that imaginable, the Buccaneers would be looking to collect a win against the Detroit Lions in week 11. Can Bucky Irving, Baker Mayfield, and the Bucs’ bodacious defense pull together to upset Dan Campbell’s bunch on the road? First Quarter: It was Baker Mayfield’s ball first on Sunday and it was his chance to get sacked first— One play, three defenders getting off their blocks, and one sack of Baker Mayfield with a forced fumble to boot. The Bucs stayed in possession only to punt and play defense. Jared Goff’s second pass and first completion of the day took Detroit across midfield, but two batted balls in a three play sequence forced the Lions into a long field attempt and long field goal miss. The Buccaneers’ offense found a few completions, a few third down conversions, and more importantly a bit of their stride. Tampa Bay moved nearly 50 yards to the Detroit 10-yard line before having to make a decision. Facing a fourth and one, Todd Bowles neglected a short field goal opportunity and chose to leave his offense on the field. Zac Robinson opted for Bucky Irving running into traffic and that traffic did more than slow him down, it stopped him. Tampa’s failed fourth down attempt jump started Detroit’s next drive. Second Quarter: 50% of Tampa’s star cornerback tandem would leave the field on Detroit’s second drive and for Todd Bowles’ defense, no Parrish = no good. The Lions tagged Benjamin Morrison for a big play and tagged him again for a touchdown. While Morrison did struggle to fill the Jacob Parrish’s shoes, one of the early death nails for Tampa’s defense though the early moments has been thorough inability to keep the Lions out of third down and one and a subsequent inability to stop Detroit from converting those third downs into first downs. 7-0, Lions. Tampa’s next start was kicked off by a false start— No doubt they had been holding that in, going an entire quarter without one. The Bucs’ next drive no longer featured third down as an unconquerable foe third downs— First down Cade Otton, first down Chris Godwin, however, old habits die hard— All out blitz, sack, punt. With the seems as open as a 7/11 in New York City, Jared Goff picked apart Tampa Bay’s zones all the way into the final two minutes of the half and field goal range. 10-0, Lions. Rocking a bad thumb, a bad foot, and a bad offense Baker Mayfield had a 1:30 from the 35-yard line to cut into the Lions’ lead. One more big scramble from the Buccaneers’ injured quarterback and rare down the field throw to Bucky Irving planted Tampa Bay squarely in Chase McLaughlin’s range. The Buccaneers did not choose to settle, they took a shot at the end zone, trying for six.

(Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Knee deep in the midst of one of the most surreal playoff races that imaginable, the Buccaneers would be looking to collect a win against the Detroit Lions in week 11. Can Bucky Irving, Baker Mayfield, and the Bucs’ bodacious defense pull together to upset Dan Campbell’s bunch on the road? The Bucs stayed in possession only to punt and play defense. Jared Goff’s second pass and first completion of the day took Detroit across midfield, but two batted balls in a three play sequence forced the Lions into a long field attempt and long field goal miss. The Buccaneers’ offense found a few completions, a few third down conversions, and more importantly a bit of their stride. Tampa Bay moved nearly 50 yards to the Detroit 10-yard line before having to make a decision. Facing a fourth and one, Todd Bowles neglected a short field goal opportunity and chose to leave his offense on the field. Zac Robinson opted for Bucky Irving running into traffic and that traffic did more than slow him down, it stopped him. Tampa’s failed fourth down attempt jump started Detroit’s next drive. Second Quarter: 50% of Tampa’s star cornerback tandem would leave the field on Detroit’s second drive and for Todd Bowles’ defense, no Parrish = no good. The Lions tagged Benjamin Morrison for a big play and tagged him again for a touchdown. While Morrison did struggle to fill the Jacob Parrish’s shoes, one of the early death nails for Tampa’s defense though the early moments has been thorough inability to keep the Lions out of third down and one and a subsequent inability to stop Detroit from converting those third downs into first downs. 7-0, Lions. Tampa’s next start was kicked off by a false start— No doubt they had been holding that in, going an entire quarter without one. The Bucs’ next drive no longer featured third down as an unconquerable foe third downs— First down Cade Otton, first down Chris Godwin, however, old habits die hard— All out blitz, sack, punt. With the seems as open as a 7/11 in New York City, Jared Goff picked apart Tampa Bay’s zones all the way into the final two minutes of the half and field goal range. 10-0, Lions. Rocking a bad thumb, a bad foot, and a bad offense Baker Mayfield had a 1:30 from the 35-yard line to cut into the Lions’ lead. One more big scramble from the Buccaneers’ injured quarterback and rare down the field throw to Bucky Irving planted Tampa Bay squarely in Chase McLaughlin’s range. The Buccaneers did not choose to settle, they took a shot at the end zone, trying for six. Baker Mayfield reared back and lofted a beautiful drop into the bucket to Ted Hurst III for a 23-yard touchdown strike. Hurst III’s second grab of the drive gave the Bucs’ a feeling of what could be, in a season where deep passes or a passing game with any consistent at all has been a needle in hay stack, Ted Hurst III’s score before half flashed a glimmer of what it could be if it all ever clicked. 10-7, Detroit. Third Quarter: Following a Detroit punt, the Buccaneers’ offense had the chance to capitalize on their end of half success— They did not. Their drive began with an 80-yard touchdown scamper by Bucky Irving (called back for a Luke Goedeke hold) and ended with a punt. After coming mere moments away from holding a lead over the Detroit Lions, the Bucs were back on defense and still trailing. Once again, no Parrish = no good. Jameson Williams ran by Benjamin Morrison like Ferrari passing a Hyundai at a stop light. Williams’ score gave the Lions their largest lead of the day (10 points)— 17-7, home town team. 8:56 left in the third, down 10, plenty of time to rally— Also plenty of time for a close game to become a rout. In a pinch, the Buccaneers’ offense turned to their backs. Bucky Irving on the ground and Kenny Gainwell through the air maneuvered Zac Robinson’s offense down the field and into the end zone for a second touchdown of the day— Bucky Irving’s score brought the Buccaneers back to whin three. 17-14, team awkwardly dressed like a Carolina Panthers spin off. Fourth Quarter: The game’s final 15 minutes were Detroit’s to start. Tampa’s defense notched their first sack of the day in order to force Detroit into a punt. Pinned deep at the nine, the Bucs needed some Mayfield magic to flip the scoreboard— Somebody might’ve miscalculated the formula on the magic because the Buccaneers finished their drive with a punt, a bad punt at that. Easy does it for the Lions’ offense, smooth sailing into the end zone for another touchdown— 24-14, Lions. With 5:24 remaining in the game, the Bucs found Emeka Egbuka to pick up a first down. That would be the only first down they would earn because Tampa Bay’s offense (in 2026) is to sacks like sand is to a beach. Tampa Bay’s turnover on downs segued into a nice undisciplined brawl (discipline falls on the coach) headed by Vita Vea and the Buccaneer’s weekly collapse was complete— Seven more points for Jahmyr Gibbs, 31-14, not Todd Bowles’ team. A hurt, beat down Baker Mayfield rallied the troops for one last gasp of air. Just under two minutes to go and the Bucs road penalty flags down to the red zone and Ted Hurst III across the goal line. 31-21, Detroit.

item.title: Saints fall to 3-7 after loss to Chicago
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Travis Etienne Jr. #3 of the New Orleans Saints runs for a first down during the second quarter against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints stayed in the game against the Chicago Bears, but it just wasn’t enough as Kellen Moore’s squad dropped their third of the last four games. Following today’s loss, the Saints are now 3-7 on the season and sit in last place in the NFC South. Saints Scoring QB Tyler Shough 1-yard passing touchdown to RB Alvin Kamara The veteran back continued his scoring form to get the black and gold on the board, having gone down 16-0 early. K Charlie Smyth – 56-yard field goal Having missed a kick earlier in the quarter, Smyth makes it a one-score game with the final play of the first half. K Charlie Smyth – 51-yard field goal Smyth adds another late in the game. Team Stats Passing Offense : 25/43, 187 yards, 1 touchdown, 1 interception, 6 sacks Rushing Offense: 22 attempts, 120 yards, 5.5 yards per carry Passing Defense: 15/23, 165 yards, 2 touchdowns Rushing Defense: 33 attempts, 146 yards, 4.4 yards per carry Turnovers: 2 Forced Turnovers: 2 Penalties: 7-30 Third-Down Efficiency: 8-17 Player Stats QB Tyler Shough: 25/42, 222 passing yards, 1 touchdown, 1 interception, 3 carries, 34 rushing yards WR Chris Olave: 9 receptions, 102 receiving yards WR Devaughn Vele: 7 receptions, 76 receiving yards RB Travis Etienne: 14 carries, 76 rushing yards RB Alvin Kamara: 1 reception, 1 receiving yard, 1 receiving touchdown, 1 carry, 1 rushing yard LB Danny Stutsman: 9 tackles, 3 solo, 1 interception S Jonas Sanker: 1 sack, 7 tackles, 4 solo, 1 TFL DL Colby Wooden: 1 sack, 4 tackles, 3 solo Next up: @ Bengals The Saints face another huge test on the road with a visit to Cincinnati next week.
