item.title: Connor Hellebuyck Hid the Winnipeg Jets’ Biggest Problem for Years. Kyle Connor Is Doing It Again
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kyle Connor has scored 19 of the Winnipeg Jets’ 75 goals this season. That’s 25.3% of the team’s offense through 24 games, which is a pretty ridiculous number for one player to be responsible for. It’s also the sort of statistic that should make Jets fans a little uncomfortable. Connor is doing his job. He’s one of the NHL’s best goal scorers, he’s scoring like one, and nobody is going to complain about having a player who can put the puck in the net almost whenever he feels like it. But when one guy is responsible for more than a quarter of your goals, you have to wonder what happens when he stops scoring at this pace. For Jets fans, this should sound familiar. They spent years watching Connor Hellebuyck turn games the Jets had no business winning into two points in the standings. Sometimes the Jets were genuinely excellent. Other nights, Hellebuyck was the reason nobody cared that they weren’t. The results were great. The problem was figuring out how much of that success was sustainable without him. Now Hellebuyck is in New Jersey, Connor is doing his best to carry the offense, and the Jets are still having trouble controlling play at five-on-five. The more you dig into the team’s numbers from the past several seasons, the harder it becomes to ignore just how much Hellebuyck was making up for. Hellebuyck Was Outperforming Expectations Even When the Jets Weren’t There’s a statistic from the Jets’ 2022-23 season that deserves a lot more attention than it’s received. The Jets finished that year with a plus-11 goal differential at five-on-five, slightly worse than their expected differential of plus-11.55. Nothing especially remarkable there. They scored about as many goals relative to their opponents as the quality of chances suggested they should have. Except Hellebuyck personally saved 22.46 goals above expected. That’s 22.46 goals he prevented beyond what the quality of chances he faced would predict, and the Jets still finished slightly below their expected goal differential as a team. It wasn’t the only time. In 2021-22, the Jets finished 4.95 goals below their expected differential despite Hellebuyck saving 6.28 goals above expected. In 2025-26, the team finished 0.89 goals below expected while Hellebuyck saved another 9.42. Three seasons in which the Jets failed to outperform their expected goal differential despite their starting goaltender beating expectations individually. And when the rest of the team was playing well? That’s when things got ridiculous. The Jets’ Presidents’ Trophy Season Wasn’t Quite What It Looked Like The 2024-25 Jets won 56 games, finished first overall and had the NHL’s best power play. Hellebuyck won the Hart and Vezina trophies, Mark Scheifele scored 39 goals and Connor recorded 97 points. It was the best regular season in Jets 2.0 history, and anybody trying to dismiss 56 wins is being silly. But the Jets’ five-on-five results were considerably better than their underlying number
item.content:encoded: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kyle Connor has scored 19 of the Winnipeg Jets’ 75 goals this season. That’s 25.3% of the team’s offense through 24 games, which is a pretty ridiculous number for one player to be responsible for. It’s also the sort of statistic that should make Jets fans a little uncomfortable. Connor is doing his job. He’s one of the NHL’s best goal scorers, he’s scoring like one, and nobody is going to complain about having a player who can put the puck in the net almost whenever he feels like it. But when one guy is responsible for more than a quarter of your goals, you have to wonder what happens when he stops scoring at this pace. For Jets fans, this should sound familiar. They spent years watching Connor Hellebuyck turn games the Jets had no business winning into two points in the standings. Sometimes the Jets were genuinely excellent. Other nights, Hellebuyck was the reason nobody cared that they weren’t. The results were great. The problem was figuring out how much of that success was sustainable without him. Now Hellebuyck is in New Jersey, Connor is doing his best to carry the offense, and the Jets are still having trouble controlling play at five-on-five. The more you dig into the team’s numbers from the past several seasons, the harder it becomes to ignore just how much Hellebuyck was making up for. Hellebuyck Was Outperforming Expectations Even When the Jets Weren’t There’s a statistic from the Jets’ 2022-23 season that deserves a lot more attention than it’s received. The Jets finished that year with a plus-11 goal differential at five-on-five, slightly worse than their expected differential of plus-11.55. Nothing especially remarkable there. They scored about as many goals relative to their opponents as the quality of chances suggested they should have. Except Hellebuyck personally saved 22.46 goals above expected. That’s 22.46 goals he prevented beyond what the quality of chances he faced would predict, and the Jets still finished slightly below their expected goal differential as a team. It wasn’t the only time. In 2021-22, the Jets finished 4.95 goals below their expected differential despite Hellebuyck saving 6.28 goals above expected. In 2025-26, the team finished 0.89 goals below expected while Hellebuyck saved another 9.42. Three seasons in which the Jets failed to outperform their expected goal differential despite their starting goaltender beating expectations individually. And when the rest of the team was playing well? That’s when things got ridiculous. The Jets’ Presidents’ Trophy Season Wasn’t Quite What It Looked Like The 2024-25 Jets won 56 games, finished first overall and had the NHL’s best power play. Hellebuyck won the Hart and Vezina trophies, Mark Scheifele scored 39 goals and Connor recorded 97 points. It was the best regular season in Jets 2.0 history, and anybody trying to dismiss 56 wins is being silly. But the Jets’ five-on-five results were considerably better than their underlying numbers. According to Natural Stat Trick , the Jets controlled 52.44% of expected goals that season. That’s good. A team consistently generating better chances than it allows is usually doing something right. Their actual share of goals was 58.82%. The Jets outscored opponents 170-119 at five-on-five, giving them a plus-51 goal differential despite an expected differential of plus-16.34. They finished 34.66 goals better than expected, and the previous season was even more extreme. In 2023-24, the Jets’ expected goal differential was plus-8.81. Their actual differential was plus-57. Over those two seasons, the Jets outscored opponents by 108 goals at five-on-five despite an expected goal differential of just plus-25.15. That’s 82.85 more goals in actual differential than expected. You might assume Connor, Scheifele and the rest of the Jets’ talented forwards were simply finishing their chances at an absurd rate. Except the team scored just 3.91 more goals than expected in 2023-24 and 5.52 fewer than expected in 2024-25. Across those two seasons, the Jets’ offense actually finished slightly below its expected output. The massive difference between their expected and actual goal differential came from keeping the puck out of the net. The Jets allowed 44.28 fewer goals than expected in 2023-24 and another 40.18 fewer in 2024-25. Hellebuyck personally saved 30.53 goals above expected in the first season and 35.66 in the second. Apr 13, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Winnipeg Jets center Adam Lowry (17) breaks up a scoring chance by Vegas Golden Knights left wing Ivan Barbashev (49) as goaltender Connor Hellebuyck (37) defends his net during the third period at T-Mobile Arena. Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images That last number is almost comical when you put it next to the team’s results. During the Presidents’ Trophy season, Hellebuyck saved 35.66 goals above expected at five-on-five. The Jets’ entire goal differential exceeded expectations by 34.66. His individual goaltending overperformance was larger than the team’s overall goal-differential overperformance. The Jets were a good team getting the results of a great one, thanks in large part to one of the best goaltenders in the world playing like it. The Jets Had the Talent. They Just Couldn’t Sustain the Results None of this means the Jets spent the Hellebuyck era getting dominated every night. They had some excellent lines, especially during their Presidents’ Trophy season. Connor, Scheifele and Gabriel Vilardi generated 53.39% of expected goals in more than 900 minutes together in 2024-25. Nikolaj Ehlers, Vladislav Namestnikov and Cole Perfetti controlled 52.83%, while Mason Appleton, Adam Lowry and Nino Niederreiter finished at 52.18%. Three lines controlling more than half of expected goals is exactly what you’d want from a contender. The Jets had the personnel to play good hockey without needing their goaltender to steal every game. The problem was maintaining that level of play consistently. In 2025-26, Connor, Scheifele and Vilardi generated just 46.88% of expected goals across more than 625 minutes together. Their actual goal share was still 53.09%. They were getting outchanced in terms of quality but winning the goal battle anyway. That’s wonderful when it happens, especially when you’ve got players capable of finishing chances most guys wouldn’t. It’s just not a great foundation to build your entire season around. The Jets won 52 games in 2023-24 before the Colorado Avalanche knocked them out in five. The following year, they won 56 games, needed seven to get past the St. Louis Blues and lost to the Dallas Stars in six. Having a goaltender who can make up for weaknesses is a tremendous advantage. Building a team that needs him to do it is another story, and the Jets are now asking something similar of Kyle Connor. Kyle Connor Is Giving the Jets a Familiar Problem Which brings us back to this season. Hellebuyck is gone, having been traded to the New Jersey Devils in October , and the Jets are finding out what life looks like without a perennial Vezina contender in their crease. Through 24 games, the Jets have generated just 46.85% of expected goals at five-on-five. Their actual goal share is 49.50%, meaning they’re still getting somewhat better results than the underlying chance quality would suggest, although neither number is exactly impressive. Meanwhile, Connor has scored 19 goals and is responsible for 25.3% of the Jets’ total offense. For years, Hellebuyck made it easier to overlook what the Jets weren’t doing well because they kept winning anyway. Now Connor is scoring at a pace that makes it a little easier to overlook how much trouble the team is having controlling play. There’s nothing wrong with either player being exceptional. The Jets should be thrilled to have had Hellebuyck for as long as they did, and they should enjoy every goal Connor scores this season. But wouldn’t it be nice if they didn’t need quite so mu

item.title: Saquon Barkley injured in Eagles' victory. What happened to star RB
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles ' streak-breaking victory came at a cost. Eagles running back Saquon Barkley injured his shoulder during the fourth quarter of Philadelphia's 19-16 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers Nov. 22 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. Barkley, whose last carry came with 8:02 left in the fourth quarter, rushed for 75 yards on 17 carries. He also had the Eagles' lone touchdown. Will Shipley replaced Barkley on the field. Barkley was on the sidelines with his helmet in his hand. Eagles fans react: Eagles snap losing streak as fans react on social media Greg Giesen is a trending writer for Delaware Online/The News Journal. item.title: Patriots playoff picture: Updating the postseason outlook on the bye
item.description: The New England Patriots are watching Week 11 from afar; fresh off a trip to Germany, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel is enjoying its bye. It is doing so from outside the playoff picture after dropping to 5-5 last Sunday, and will remain there. Still, with the early window of games in the books, we can see there has been some movement in the conference. And so, let’s take a look at the standings in the AFC. AFC East standings: Week 11 Buffalo Bills (9-1) New England Patriots (5-5) New York Jets (2-8) Miami Dolphins (1-9) With both now on 10 game played, it becomes even clearer just how big of an advantage the Bills have over the Patriots in the race AFC East title. On Sunday, Buffalo added a ninth victory to their tally by beating the Dolphins 26-9 and now sits a comfortable four games ahead of the reigning champions. We have said it before and it holds true this week: it would take a monumental collapse for the Bills not two take the division crown this season. The Jets will play the Chargers in the afternoon window. AFC playoff standings: Week 11 Buffalo Bills (9-1) Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) Denver Broncos (7-2) Cleveland Browns (6-4) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) On the bubble: 8. New England Patriots (5-5) , 9. Houston Texans (4- 6) , 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-6), 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-7) Not yet eliminated, but let’s be real here: 12. Indianapolis Colts (3-8), 13. New York Jets (2- 8 ), 14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) , 15. Tennessee Titans (1-9), 16. Miami Dolphins (1-9) Joe Milton, take a bow. The former Patriots sixth-round draft pick, who was later traded to Dallas and is currently serving as the Eagles’ starting quarterback, helped his team upset the Steelers 19-16. While Pittsburgh still remains ahead of New England in the standings, there are now two teams well within reach considering that the Patriots currently hold all important tiebreakers over both the Steelers (head-to-head) and Browns (conference record, strength of victory, strength of schedule). Obviously, the Patriots will need to do their part in order to catch at least one of the two wild card competitors, but Pittsburgh losing is still a positive development.

item.title: Ravens discussion: instant reactions to rollercoaster loss to Panthers
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens lost their sixth straight game on Sunday afternoon, falling to the Carolina Panthers by a score of 35-33. A back-and-forth matchup came down to the final drives, and once again, Baltimore’s defense could not get off the field during a late drive with the game on the line. Carolina took a two-point lead, setting Jacoby Brissett up for a potential game-winning score. Instead, he faced constant pressure in the pocket and had to throw up a prayer to avoid a sack that resulted in a game-ending interception. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the loss: Nikhil Mehta This game was drunk from the very start. The Ravens made their usual mistakes in all three phases – missed tackles, poor clock management, inept pass protection – but the Panthers tried to outdo them at every turn. There aren’t really any new takeaways. As in 2025, this team has been screaming at us, all year, that this is who they are. Jesse Minter’s Ravens simply cannot be at their best when the best is needed. In my opinion, their best is no longer needed. At 4-7, the season is effectively over. Winning out to snag a playoff spot – if that is even possible – is far-fetched even if Lamar Jackson comes back against the Steelers in Week 15. In fact, far-fetched might not be far enough. Baltimore is playing for a top-10 draft pick at this point. Maybe top-five. Kevin McNelis It almost feels worse to have the game be winnable at this point than to have the Ravens just get blown out. They had another double-digit lead, albeit early, which they squandered with miserable pass defense and multiple turnovers. Same stuff, different day. Now they have to worry about any lasting effects from a Derrick Henry concussion. At least Mike Green has started to show up big time. I like what I’m seeing from him, and if the Ravens can get Tavius Robinson to come back, they could have a pair of young EDGEs that would make it easier to build forward. Stephen Bopst It was simply another comedy of errors in Charlotte today. The Ravens continued their downward spiral by committing multiple errors that put a nail in their season. Justice Hill fumbled the ball out of the end zone, LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts, Derrick Henry fumbled, and to top it off Jacoby Brissett threw an awful game-ending pick. The Ravens were in position to win each of the last two games on the final drive but predictably gave the ball to the other team. Obviously, I want the Ravens to win, but continued losing is probably what it will take for some bigger changes to occur this off-season. Amongst all the other issues this year, I really am not seeing a lot of hope for the Jesse Minter led Ravens in the future. At the bare minimum, he was supposed to give this defense a boost which hasn’t come. Is it the players fault too? Yes, but I’ve seen a lot of other defensive coaches do a lot more with a lot less over the years. While I assume the front office will give Minter a grace year to build the defense with

item.title: 5 takeaways from Lions’ 31-21 win against Bucs
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Chuck Clark #36 of the Detroit Lions steps over Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after a sack during the second quarter of the NFL football game at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions returned to Ford Field on a five-game winning streak entering Week 11. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers flew up and put up a fight, but it wasn’t enough, and they lost 31-21. The first half was low-scoring, but the offense exploded in the second half, and Tampa Bay couldn’t overcome it. Here are my five takeaways from the Lions’ victory against the Buccaneers. Front seven balled out We saw it against the Patriots last week, and again against the Bucs this week. Just because EDGE Aidan Hutchinson is out doesn’t mean this defensive line can’t still bring the juice. On the very first play of the game, Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield got rocked and fumbled the ball on a sack by EDGE DJ Wonnum. DJ Wonnum starting the game off with the sack! pic.twitter.com/l1aqtbRDs0 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 Mayfield faced pressure often, and he was more mobile than I expected with the foot injury, which made life more difficult for the Lions’ front seven. EDGE Derrick Moore continues to play at a high level, recording his fifth sack of the season. It wasn’t just the defensive line getting to Mayfield either, as linebacker Trevor Nowaske got a huge sack in the fourth quarter to help put this game out of reach for the Bucs. They also did a fair job with their run fits, holding Bucs running back Bucky Irving to 68 yards on 18 carries. It was strong in the first half, but just as the Bucs may have started to run on Detroit, the Lions got a lead too big for them to keep leaning on him to move the ball down the field. The tight ends found some exploits Every tight end for Detroit got involved on Sunday afternoon. The biggest name was Sam LaPorta, who finished with three catches for 62 yards. He was looked at often and helped move the chains most through the air. Just because LaPorta was targeted didn’t mean the others were forgotten. Backup Brock Wright had two catches for 42 yards, and third-string Tyler Conklin had an 18-yard catch. It was a day where the 12 and 13 personnel got their chances, and Tampa Bay couldn’t figure it out early on. Detroit was using them heavily and went away from it, which was odd. Usually, this offense finds a weakness and exploits it, and they seemed to take their foot off the gas in the second half. Shoutout K.J. Britt and Chuck Clark Before the season started, I wouldn’t have thought linebacker K.J. Britt and safety Chuck Clark would be helpful depth pieces on this team, but here we are. Britt was recently signed off the New England Patriots practice squad and was considered for intel in Week 10. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions returned to Ford Field on a five-game winning streak entering Week 11. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers flew up and put up a fight, but it wasn’t enough, and they lost 31-21. Just because EDGE Aidan Hutchinson is out doesn’t mean this defensive line can’t still bring the juice. On the very first play of the game, Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield got rocked and fumbled the ball on a sack by EDGE DJ Wonnum. DJ Wonnum starting the game off with the sack! pic.twitter.com/l1aqtbRDs0 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 Mayfield faced pressure often, and he was more mobile than I expected with the foot injury, which made life more difficult for the Lions’ front seven. EDGE Derrick Moore continues to play at a high level, recording his fifth sack of the season. It wasn’t just the defensive line getting to Mayfield either, as linebacker Trevor Nowaske got a huge sack in the fourth quarter to help put this game out of reach for the Bucs. They also did a fair job with their run fits, holding Bucs running back Bucky Irving to 68 yards on 18 carries. It was strong in the first half, but just as the Bucs may have started to run on Detroit, the Lions got a lead too big for them to keep leaning on him to move the ball down the field. The tight ends found some exploits Every tight end for Detroit got involved on Sunday afternoon. The biggest name was Sam LaPorta, who finished with three catches for 62 yards. He was looked at often and helped move the chains most through the air. Just because LaPorta was targeted didn’t mean the others were forgotten. Backup Brock Wright had two catches for 42 yards, and third-string Tyler Conklin had an 18-yard catch. It was a day where the 12 and 13 personnel got their chances, and Tampa Bay couldn’t figure it out early on. Detroit was using them heavily and went away from it, which was odd. Usually, this offense finds a weakness and exploits it, and they seemed to take their foot off the gas in the second half. Shoutout K.J. Britt and Chuck Clark Before the season started, I wouldn’t have thought linebacker K.J. Britt and safety Chuck Clark would be helpful depth pieces on this team, but here we are. Britt was recently signed off the New England Patriots practice squad and was considered for intel in Week 10. He got some playing time against Tampa Bay and made some crucial tackles when the team needed it, finishing with four tackles, one for a loss. Clark was seen as a potential starter with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph out at the start of the year. With Branch and now Joseph back, Clark was seen as the odd man out, but not for long, as Clark was promoted to a team captain and got the green dot on his helmet. Clark got a sack on Mayfield on Sunday, recorded eight tackles and had a pass deflection. Players like Britt and Clark stepping up when needed are good to see, and show how much depth this team has all over. If one of Detroit’s best players is down, it’s a next-man-up mentality, and those players don’t let those chances slip. I love you Jamo, but don’t do that again You’d think after what happened last week with Hutchinson’s injury, the players would be more careful with their celebrations. Wide receiver Jameson Williams didn’t hear what head coach Dan Campbell said earlier in the week about players not flipping for celebrations. Williams is a fun character, and I get he brings a lot of energy to the team, but after what just happened to Hutchinson, it should’ve been a reminder not to be too crazy. Jameson Williams’ front flip celly 😭 (📺 Fox) pic.twitter.com/HWAARWtR2c — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 22, 2026 Despite a slow start, Gibbs has a strong performance Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was struggling to start the game, and it made sense; the Bucs defense is one of the best in the NFL. They’ve held teams to 79 rushing yards a game and have allowed the league’s fewest rushing touchdowns in three. Gibbs met a wall and had few successful runs early, but after the Lions’ passing game took over, the lanes opened up for him. Gibbs finished with 23 carries for 98 yards and two touchdowns, along with four catches for 20 yards. He not only scored twice against the Bucs, but he’s now tied with Lions legend Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns before turning 25. Jahmyr Gibbs vs Buccaneers: 23 CAR 98 YDS 2 TD Ties Barry Sanders for the most RUSH TD before turning 25. pic.twitter.com/EwfNSmUBjz — StatMuse (@statmuse) November 22, 2026 There are seven games left this season, and this is just another record for Gibbs to run up and make it even tougher for someone to break. Gibbs won’t be 25 until March, so he will have the final seven games to run up that total. He continues to tie or break records, with plenty of time to make it even crazier for him to win, at the very least, NFL Offensive Player of the Year, but again, he is showing MVP tendencies.

item.title: Here’s where the Falcons currently stand in the NFC South, the NFL’s weirdest division
item.description: Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images | Getty Images The Falcons are on their bye this week, but play continued in Week 11 for the rest of the NFC South — and it did shake up the standings a bit in a good way for the Falcons. The Panthers were the only NFC South team to win on Sunday, escaping with a narrow 2-point win over the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens and moving their record to 5-5. Carolina stays on top of the NFC South, and thanks to the other two teams losing, the Panthers extend their division lead to two games. The Buccaneers were facing the Lions in Detroit, and they lost 31-21. The Saints faced off against the Chicago Bears, and they lost 13-21. That evens up the Bucs, Saints, and Falcons at 3-7 through 11 weeks, and thanks to Atlanta’s head-to-head tiebreaker over New Orleans, the Saints drop down to the basement of this weird division. The Falcons are still eligible for the 2026 NFL playoffs, though I would not hold your breath. Fanduel Sportsbook has Atlanta’s odds to make the playoffs at +700, and while the Panthers’ two-game lead isn’t insurmountable with seven games left to play, I don’t think anyone who’s watched the Falcons play over the past few weeks is holding their breath for that outcome. NFC South standings after Week 11 Carolina Panthers 5-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers 3-7 Atlanta Falcons 3-7 New Orleans Saints 3-7 NFC playoff picture after Week 11 San Francisco 49ers 8-1 Detroit Lions 8-2 New York Giants 5-3-1 Carolina Panthers 5-5 Chicago Bears 8-2 Minnesota Vikings 7-2 Green Bay Packers 6-4 In the hunt: Seattle Seahawks 6-4 Los Angeles Rams 6-4 Dallas Cowboys 5-6 Washington Commanders 3-5-1 Tampa Bay Buccaneers 3-7 Atlanta Falcons 3-7 New Orleans Saints 3-7 Philadelphia Eagles 3-7 Arizona Cardinals 3-8

item.title: Pepe did not injure eyes staring at sun, say Villarreal
item.description: Nicolas Pepe (right) wore an eye mask on his return to the side following his eye operation in October [Getty Images] Villarreal say reports striker Nicolas Pepe needed eye surgery because he stared directly at the solar eclipse are "completely false". In a statement, the Spanish club said an operation in October that ruled the 31-year-old out for six matches was "scheduled in advance" and "entirely unrelated" to the eclipse, which took place on 12 August. Reports on social media suggested the former Arsenal forward had injured his eyes staring directly at the sun during the lunar event, with a video then emerging - purportedly from one of Pepe's social media accounts - showing him watching it in Spain. "Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe's eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse," said the club. "The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event. "The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players' health." Staring at an eclipse without protection can damage the retina, which sits at the back of the eye, and particularly those cells responsible for sharp central vision. In the build-up to this summer's event, experts warned only genuine specially-designed solar eclipse glasses should be used, and that ordinary sunglasses or other devices were not enough to prevent potential damage. Pepe has scored 14 goals in 86 appearances in all competitions for Villarreal after joining from Trabzonspor in 2024. He cost Arsenal a then-club record £72m when he joined from Lille in the summer of 2019. Pepe scored 27 goals in 112 games for the Gunners and had a loan spell at Nice before joining Trabzonspor on a free transfer. Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast

item.description: TARRYTOWN, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 23: Head coach Mike Brown of the New York Knicks speaks to the media at Knicks Training Facility on September 23, 2025 in Tarrytown, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) The New York Knicks are back in action Sunday after a thrilling victory over the Portland Trail Blazers last night. Without multiple key stars in the lineup, the Knicks took command early before the Blazers stormed back and pushed the home team to the absolute brink. With New York down two in the final seconds of game, it was star forward Mikal Bridges — not Jalen Brunson — who took one dribble, stepped back into a shot and canned a 3-pointer to win the Knicks their 10th game of the season. Knicks Need More Hero Work From Bridges, Brunson to Knock Off Pacers Getty NEW YORK, NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 11: Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks shoots against the Cleveland Cavaliers during their game at Madison Square Garden on November 11, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) New York was without stars Karl-Anthony Towns and OG Anunoby and reserve guard Jordan Clarkson on Friday, making their win over the Blazers, who entered the game with more wins on the season, even more impressive. Towns, 30, was ruled out with an illness, while Anunoby, 28, was sidelined with left calf tightness. Ahead of Sunday’s contest, the Knicks revealed that Anunoby will miss the second game in a row, while Towns, who is still battling an illness, has been listed as questionable. Clarkson, who is dealing with a right plantar fasciitis, is out again and will miss his third game in a row. While injuries are unfortunate, the Knicks have begun to click following an alarming 0-3 start. The play of Towns and Anunoby has been instrumental in the team’s turnaround, which is why the team will have a steep uphill climb until both stars return. The good news is that New York has won four games in a row, with multiple coming down to the wire. Without Towns, who is having one of the best seasons of his 12-year career, and Anunoby, more of the onus will fall onto Brunson and Bridges. While Brunson is putting up MVP-caliber numbers once again, scoring 30 points and cashing six 3-pointers in Friday’s narrow win, Bridges has slowly started to look like his old self. item.content:encoded: TARRYTOWN, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 23: Head coach Mike Brown of the New York Knicks speaks to the media at Knicks Training Facility on September 23, 2025 in Tarrytown, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Dustin Satloff/Getty Images) Getty NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 11: Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks shoots against the Cleveland Cavaliers during their game at Madison Square Garden on November 11, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) The New York Knicks are back in action Sunday after a thrilling victory over the Portland Trail Blazers last night. Without multiple key stars in the lineup, the Knicks took command early before the Blazers stormed back and pushed the home team to the absolute brink. With New York down two in the final seconds of game, it was star forward Mikal Bridges — not Jalen Brunson — who took one dribble, stepped back into a shot and canned a 3-pointer to win the Knicks their 10th game of the season. Knicks Need More Hero Work From Bridges, Brunson to Knock Off Pacers Getty NEW YORK, NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 11: Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks shoots against the Cleveland Cavaliers during their game at Madison Square Garden on November 11, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) New York was without stars Karl-Anthony Towns and OG Anunoby and reserve guard Jordan Clarkson on Friday, making their win over the Blazers, who entered the game with more wins on the season, even more impressive. Towns, 30, was ruled out with an illness, while Anunoby, 28, was sidelined with left calf tightness. Ahead of Sunday’s contest, the Knicks revealed that Anunoby will miss the second game in a row, while Towns, who is still battling an illness, has been listed as questionable. Clarkson, who is dealing with a right plantar fasciitis, is out again and will miss his third game in a row. While injuries are unfortunate, the Knicks have begun to click following an alarming 0-3 start. The play of Towns and Anunoby has been instrumental in the team’s turnaround, which is why the team will have a steep uphill climb until both stars return. The good news is that New York has won four games in a row, with multiple coming down to the wire. Without Towns, who is having one of the best seasons of his 12-year career, and Anunoby, more of the onus will fall onto Brunson and Bridges. While Brunson is putting up MVP-caliber numbers once again, scoring 30 points and cashing six 3-pointers in Friday’s narrow win, Bridges has slowly started to look like his old self. In the win over Portland, the nine-year veteran recorded 12 points, with his final three points the most valuable of the night. item.title: Dayton Flyers play at Tennessee Tech in FCS Playoffs
item.description: Photo from: Nebyat Mamo/Staff Nebyat Mamo/Staff The University of Dayton football team learned its opponent in the Football Championship Subdivision (FCS) Playoffs. [DOWNLOAD: Free WHIO-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] Dayton will play the No. 11 seed Tennessee Tech on Nov. 28 in Cookeville, Tennessee. The winner plays No. 6 Youngstown in the Second Round on Dec. 5. This is UD’s second appearance in the FCS Playoffs. Their last was back in 2015 when they hosted Western Illinois and lost, 24-7. TRENDING STORIES: Can you help? Park rangers looking for people connected to ongoing investigation Tom Jackson, former Broncos star and ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’ analyst, dead at 75 1 hospitalized after accidental shooting in Butler Township The team watched as the 24-team bracket was announced on an FCS Selection Show at Boesch Lounge inside UD Arena on Sunday. The Flyers clinched an automatic bid after winning the Pioneer Football League (PFL) regular season. They clinched it with a 27-11 win over Presbyterian in Clinton, South Carolina. Dayton shares the PFL title with Butler but earned the head-to-head tiebreaker by beating the Bulldogs, 19-9 , on Oct. 17. UD has won its league-leading 13 th PFL championship. Tennessee Tech went 9-3 and finished in second place in the Southern Conference. Both UD and Tennessee Tech have played Eastern Kentucky. The Golden Eagles beat EKU, 49-20. The Flyers defeated Eastern Kentucky, 17-14. This will be the first-ever meeting between Dayton and Tennessee Tech. The Flyers’ last postseason victory came in the 1991 Division III playoffs, when they beat St. John’s 19-7 in the third round. Larry Hansgen and Mike Kelly broadcast Saturday’s FCS Playoff game between Dayton and Tennessee Tech on WHIO Radio . [SIGN UP: WHIO-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ]

item.title: Greenwich dethrones Staples on PKs in epic CIAC Class LL boys soccer championship
item.description: Members of the Greenwich boys soccer team celebrate after defeating Staples 3-2 (4-1 PKs) for the CAC Class LL championship on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026 at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford. (Will Aldam/Hearst Connecticut Media) HARTFORD - There was only one team expected to stay on its high horse as a CIAC boys soccer champion at Trinity Health Stadium this weekend. Only one team had a chance. That was Staples, a team even the opposing coach conceded was the best side in the state. But you know how things can go in the Wild West of sports. The plot can flip, the script riddled with holes, even high noon runs on to 3 p.m. Greenwich emerged as the new sheriff of Class LL boys soccer Sunday afternoon, knocking off top-seeded and defending champion Staples 3-2, on penalty kicks. The No. 6 Cardinals erased a 2-0 deficit in the second half and then dominated PKs 4-1, hitting all four of their shots while goalie Oliver Almeida turned two Staples attempts aside. It was the third state championship for Greenwich (15-4-3) and the team's first since 2022. Greenwich lost to Staples 3-0 in last year's final and the Wreckers (21-1-1) were undefeated going into their title defense. A 14th state title seemed fated when the Wreckers sprung to a 2-0 lead on a penalty kick by Adrian Rodriguez and a goal from Noah Rossoni. But Greenwich cut the deficit in half on a goal by MVP Shaun Liu with 26 minutes to play and Ebrima Touray delivered the equalizer with just over five minutes to go. After a scoreless overtime, Greenwich went 4-for-4 at the PK line behind Luca Ferrario, Sonny Warsing, Charlie Maniaci and Landon McFerran, while Almeida stopped two of the three attempts by Staples. Warsing and McFerran hadn't even been on the field during regulation and overtime, but when their number was called by coach Kurt Putnam, they were ready, and when McFerran drove home the fourth tally for Greenwich, it was over. Earlier, a Staples repeat seemed preordained. Just 5:25 in. Staples rushed the box, Almeida charged out and the ensuing contact resulted in a yellow card for Almeida and a penalty kick for Staples. The yellow card sent Almeida to the bench for the play and brought Logan Musumeci in to face Staples' Adrian Rodriguez 12 yards away. Could there be a tougher ask? Musumeci dove right. Rodrigez shot left. Staples led 1-0. Despite long odds made even steeper, Greenwich battled admirably in the wake of the PK, and the game settled into entertaining up-and-down action. Almeida, back in net, was up to the task and so was Staples counterpart Luke Diedrich at the other end. It got fast, it got physical. Greyson Downes of Staples was hit with a yellow card with 10:40 left in the half. A few minutes later, so was Liu. Meanwhile, in the goal count, Staples doubled its lead 4:41 before half. item.content:encoded: Members of the Greenwich boys soccer team celebrate after defeating Staples 3-2 (4-1 PKs) for the CAC Class LL championship on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026 at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford. (Will Aldam/Hearst Connecticut Media) HARTFORD - There was only one team expected to stay on its high horse as a CIAC boys soccer champion at Trinity Health Stadium this weekend. Only one team had a chance. That was Staples, a team even the opposing coach conceded was the best side in the state. But you know how things can go in the Wild West of sports. The plot can flip, the script riddled with holes, even high noon runs on to 3 p.m. Greenwich emerged as the new sheriff of Class LL boys soccer Sunday afternoon, knocking off top-seeded and defending champion Staples 3-2, on penalty kicks. The No. 6 Cardinals erased a 2-0 deficit in the second half and then dominated PKs 4-1, hitting all four of their shots while goalie Oliver Almeida turned two Staples attempts aside. It was the third state championship for Greenwich (15-4-3) and the team's first since 2022. Greenwich lost to Staples 3-0 in last year's final and the Wreckers (21-1-1) were undefeated going into their title defense. A 14th state title seemed fated when the Wreckers sprung to a 2-0 lead on a penalty kick by Adrian Rodriguez and a goal from Noah Rossoni. But Greenwich cut the deficit in half on a goal by MVP Shaun Liu with 26 minutes to play and Ebrima Touray delivered the equalizer with just over five minutes to go. After a scoreless overtime, Greenwich went 4-for-4 at the PK line behind Luca Ferrario, Sonny Warsing, Charlie Maniaci and Landon McFerran, while Almeida stopped two of the three attempts by Staples. Warsing and McFerran hadn't even been on the field during regulation and overtime, but when their number was called by coach Kurt Putnam, they were ready, and when McFerran drove home the fourth tally for Greenwich, it was over. Earlier, a Staples repeat seemed preordained. Just 5:25 in. Staples rushed the box, Almeida charged out and the ensuing contact resulted in a yellow card for Almeida and a penalty kick for Staples. The yellow card sent Almeida to the bench for the play and brought Logan Musumeci in to face Staples' Adrian Rodriguez 12 yards away. Could there be a tougher ask? Musumeci dove right. Rodrigez shot left. Staples led 1-0. Despite long odds made even steeper, Greenwich battled admirably in the wake of the PK, and the game settled into entertaining up-and-down action. Almeida, back in net, was up to the task and so was Staples counterpart Luke Diedrich at the other end. It got fast, it got physical. Greyson Downes of Staples was hit with a yellow card with 10:40 left in the half. A few minutes later, so was Liu. Meanwhile, in the goal count, Staples doubled its lead 4:41 before half. Rodriguez ran onto a through ball at the top of the box, encountered two Greenwich defenders and dished to Rossoni on his left. Dribbling, dekeing, Rossoni freed up space and bounded a shot into the far corner. Down 2-0, the Cards didn't fold. They continued to bid, and Liu drew the first winner, beating a defender 1-on-1 in the box and toeing a shot past Diedrich with 26:06 left in regulation. Touray's game-tying goal came with 5:20 left. He was stationed at the left post, in perfect position for the rebound that came when Diedrich made a diving stop on a liner from the top of the box off the foot of Liu. A little more than a minute later Greenwich appeared to net the go-ahead goal, again on a rebound, this one off the post, but the play was ruled offsides. Both teams had chances in OT. Both teams had corners. Greenwich put one off the side of the net. Staples couldn't finish either. Fatigue had long settled in. A number of players from both teams collapsed to the turf when the second OT expired. They got back on their feet. An epic would be decided at 12 paces. This story will be updated. Player of the Game Oliver Almeida. The Greenwich goalkeeper stopped two of the three shots he faced in penalty kicks CIAC CLASS LL BOYS SOCCER CHAMPIONSHIP Greenwich 3, Staples 2 (4-1 PKs) GREENWICH 0 2 0 0 (4)-2 STAPLES 2 0 0 0 (1)-0 Scoring: (S) Adrian Rodriguez 5:25; (S) Noah Rossoni 35:19; (G) Shaun Liu 53:54; (G) E Touray 74:40. Records: Greenwich 15-4-3; Staples 21-1-1. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. Get the biggest headlines of the day from our network of journalists around the state. item.title: Nikko Remigio’s Wife Maureen Recounts Turbulent 24 Hours After He Was Cut from the Chiefs ‘Out of the Blue’
item.description: Maureen Remigio; Nikko Remigio Credit: Maureen Remigio/Instagram;Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire NEED TO KNOW Nikko Remigio’s wife, Maureen Remigio, shared an Instagram video in which she recounted the turbulent 24 hours after he was cut from the Kansas City Chiefs “out of the blue” She detailed how their lives changed after receiving the unexpected news The Chiefs announced on Nov. 11 that they had waived Nikko, along with defensive end Jack Pyburn, after acquiring wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts NFL player Nikko Remigio’s wife, Maureen Remigio, is recounting the chaotic 24 hours the couple experienced after he was cut from the Kansas City Chiefs “out of the blue.” On Nov. 11, the Chiefs announced that they had waived the return specialist and wide receiver, along with defensive end Jack Pyburn, after acquiring wide receiver Josh Downs in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts. Two days later, the team shared a farewell post on Instagram in Nikko’s honor, writing, “From an undrafted free agent to a Super Bowl champ 🏆. Thank you for everything, @nikkoremigio!” Now, Nikko’s wife is taking her followers behind the scenes of the turbulent hours that followed his release from the team. In a candid video shared on Instagram, the influencer detailed how their “lives changed, literally in 24 hours.” Maureen, a former Philippine track and field star, began by explaining that Nikko, 27, was in the middle of his fourth season with the Chiefs when he was let go. “Out of the blue, on Tuesday afternoon [Nov. 10], we found out he was being released by the Chiefs,” she said. “We just got a text that he needs to come in, bring his iPad — and that’s it.” She continued, “I really just want to make you guys understand how quick everything happens. Once a team waives you, within 24 hours, any team can claim you and continue your contract.” Maureen said that within those 24 hours, “you don’t know where you’re going, you don’t know who’s going to get you, if you’re going to get claimed or not, and what your options are.” “So you can just imagine the waiting game, the sitting around, the walking around the house, the uncertainty that just happened in a snap of a finger,” she continued. Nikko Remigio during the Chiefs-Raiders game at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo., on Oct. 19, 2025 Credit: Jamie Squire/Getty Maureen shared that Nikko found out he had been picked up by the Houston Texans “almost close to the 24th hour.” The team had booked Nikko onto a flight to Houston that was leaving in just over two hours. “We’re 45 minutes away from the airport, so guess what? Rush, put in all the clothes you need, drove him to the airport — and just like that, he’s in Houston,” she recalled, saying she’s still “processing” the whirlwind series of events. Maureen said Nikko’s move to a new team has left the couple with a lot of difficult decisions to make, including whether she will join him in Houston right away, what to do with their house and their pets, and more. She said she has been leaning on other NFL WAGs who have been in similar situations and tapping them for advice. Maureen Remigio and Nikko Remigio at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo. Credit: Maureen Remigio/Instagram “I just picked their brains and said, ‘Help me figure this out,’ ” she explained, adding that she planned to go to Houston soon to “check things out.” Nikko made his debut with the Texans in their game against the Cleveland Browns on Nov. 15, averaging 28.5 yards on kickoff returns and 14.5 yards on punt returns, per ESPN . In her video, Maureen noted that she was sharing “a side of professional football that not a lot of people understand or see.” “There is so much uncertainty that comes with this business — and it’s a very cold business,” she said. “Sometimes you can have a job yesterday, and the next day you might not have a job. Not all athletes’ contracts are guaranteed. And Nikko, being an undrafted free agent, has always had to fight for his spot on the roster.” PEOPLE has reached out to the Kansas City Chiefs for comment. Read the original article on People

item.title: Price wins Grand Slam to end wait for major title
item.description: Gerwyn Price has won the Grand Slam of Darts four times [Press Association] Gerwyn Price ended his four-year wait for a major PDC title as he powered to a brilliant 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final. The Welshman last won a major title when he claimed the World Series in 2022, but finally got over the line after defeats in three finals in 2026. The 41-year-old was the runner-up at the World Matchplay, World Grand Prix and World Series, as well as suffering semi-final exits in the Premier League, World Masters, UK Open and European Championships. This title has been long overdue and Price won it in spectacular fashion with a mid-match burst. Despite six breaks of throw in the opening 14 legs - including brilliant 150 and 145 checkouts from Price - the game was level at 7-7. But Price claimed a crucial lead in a scrappy 15th leg when he finally took out double two at the sixth attempt. That flicked a switch after a mini-interval and Price won the next five legs to open up a six-leg advantage. Van Veen broke back after another interval, but Price was able to hold off any hopes of a comeback from the Dutchman and seal his fourth Grand Slam title. "It's amazing - I've had some close calls this year when I probably should have won games and tournaments, but when it finally comes around it's nice," Price, who moves to world number three, told Sky Sports. "I was probably more nervous in this game than ever. Just to keep the media off my back, I mean I do mind and I don't mind, but just to keep them off my back. "Now they can leave me alone!" The triumph, which sees Price earn £200,000 and the Eric Bristow Trophy, is his first in a PDC ranking and TV major since he won this event in 2021. The pair will now switch their focus to the Players Championship Finals from Friday, where they could meet in the second round. That event will determine Price's place in the PDC order of merit and his seeding for the World Championships which begin on 11 December. The draw takes place on 30 November. Reaction and analysis as Price wins Grand Slam title Grand Slam of Darts results & prize money What does this mean for the World Championship? Across the 19 editions of the Grand Slam, seven of the winners have gone on to triumph at the World Championship in the weeks that follow. It has happened in each of the past four years, with Luke Littler (twice), Luke Humphries and Michael Smith doubling up. The past 10 years have delivered five winners of both in the same season, while another two Grand Slam winners have reached the Worlds semi-finals and one the quarter-finals. Therefore a Grand Slam winner usually has a pretty decent run at the Worlds, although with Van Veen as second seed and Price either third or fourth, that would hardly be a huge surprise. item.title: Liverpool hand Pochettino nightmare Manchester United start after Yoro sees red
item.description: Green shoots of recovery have lasted longer in a blast furnace than in the Mauricio Pochettino era at ­Manchester United. On another abysmal Anfield day for the fallen giants of Manchester, Pochettino endured a baptism of fire from the eighth minute onwards when Leny Yoro was sent off for ­denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. Liverpool would not be denied anything else while tormenting their old rivals yet again. Andoni Iraola indulged in his first fist-pumps towards the Kop after an utterly dominant, comfortable win illuminated by Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz brilliance plus goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz. Liver­pool’s two creative forces were also on the scoresheet as Ngumoha became the youngster scorer in the fixture’s history. Continue reading...

item.title: McBurnie’s added-time double snatches win for Hull to shock 10-man Brighton
item.description: Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment. Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and the headline-grabbing moments , these games are the ones which can trip you up the most. Continue reading...

item.title: Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return
item.description: The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat second in the Championship table and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight. Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly. Continue reading...

item.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
item.description: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will. Continue reading...

item.title: Pochettino needs New Manager Bounce to break torrid Manchester United turnover | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Latest hire will depend on fresh faces and time to bed in at Old Trafford where the dugout churn is hardest to budge Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation. Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials. Continue reading...

item.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
item.description: New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row. Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.” Continue reading...

item.title: Teenage ace Williams-Barnett puts Tottenham on path to win over Ipswich
item.description: Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich. That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett. Continue reading...

item.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
item.description: The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality. He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session. Continue reading...

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. Continue reading...

item.title: The male footballers best associated with each shirt number – the readers’ edition
item.description: Last week we selected 50 players who are synonymous with their squad numbers . Our readers spotted notable absentees so came up with an alternative list, which does not start at No 1 or end at No 50 Which footballers are inextricably linked to their shirt numbers? We picked out 50 players last week who have come to embody the numbers on their backs. It was not an exhaustive list – as our readers have proved. We couldn’t include some legends of the game – Pelé and Lionel Messi for a start – and we missed a few brilliant stories. Thankfully our readers have provided an alternative list. item.title: Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release
item.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m. Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Football’s political gamers face off at Fifa with the real-life final boss
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world” , football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat. When I first saw the photo in yesterday’s Football Daily , I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner. That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT time will be remembered fondly, but it wasn’t transformational
item.description: The incoming Manchester United manager improved the US team’s culture and competitiveness, but could not bring about sea change in two years In a theater high up in a midtown Manhattan skyscraper built from lots of glass, a highlight reel played to deafening music. And then, on “a monumental day for US Soccer”, federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, announced they had bagged their man, Mauricio Pochettino, to become the highest-profile United States manager in the men’s national team’s history. Pochettino held court for three-quarters of an hour in his signature blend of Spanglish before the assembled media and a grab bag of sponsors. Then he recorded some TV hits. And after that, in a bit of accidental prescience, he went off to record a podcast with Gary Neville. Continue reading...

item.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
item.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...

He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds. Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons. item.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, Northern Ireland from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017. 183 places Montenegro (16th/199th) 165 Kuwait (24/189) 160 Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173) 155 Cape Verde (27/182) 153 Central African Republic (49/202) 151 Libya (36/187) 146 Equatorial Guinea (49/195) 144 Moldova (37/181) 141 El Salvador (49/190) 136 Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150) Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. Continue reading...

item.title: Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid
item.description: ‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2 . The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before. The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 win at the Azteca Stadium and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Have a question for Jonathan? Email soccerwithjw@theguardian.com , and he’ll answer the best in a future edition. Continue reading...

item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. Continue reading...

item.title: A long wait, some magic and that smile: Ronaldinho savours Ravenna debut at 46
item.description: Brazilian legend, an investor at Serie C club, showed glimpses of old brilliance as he played 45 minutes for the promotion-chasing side It may have been the longest buildup in world football. In June, the former Barcelona and Brazil legend Ronaldinho was unveiled by the Serie C side Ravenna to make his comeback at the age of 46 – 11 years after his last official game. Then silence. But on a chilly November day on the eastern coast of Italy, there he was , not only in the squad, but in the starting XI for the eagerly anticipated derby against Forlì as Ravenna chase promotion. Continue reading...
